content.text:
I've read both PDFs in full: 6 pages and 31 pages. That includes the 11 embedded images, which I cropped at 300 dpi and read visually. They contain the 3- and 4-configuration comparison tables, the architecture flow, the tech-stack table, the demo archetypes, the metric definitions, the verifier evaluation table and two HDB infographics. **I haven't written any files yet.** Below is the proposed structure and the ambiguities I need you to decide.

Two things before the proposal:
- The PDFs are named `assessment requirements.pdf` and `project approach.pdf`, with spaces, not underscores.
- The repo has no `.gitignore` and no commits yet. The PDFs aren't tracked, but nothing stops them from being added.

---

## Part 1 — Proposed documentation structure

### Conventions used in every file
- **Status tag on every item:**
  - `MANDATORY`: from the assessment brief.
  - `APPROVED`: an explicitly final decision in the project approach.
  - `PROPOSED`: a recommendation that needs your review.
  - `OPEN`: an open question.
  - `HISTORICAL`: earlier brainstorming.
  - `SUPERSEDED`: replaced by a later decision, kept with a pointer to its replacement.
- **Source citation on every item:** `[ASM p.N]` for the assessment brief and `[APP p.N]` for the project approach. `N` is the physical PDF page.
- **Content provenance labels:**
  - `COPIED-SOURCE`: verbatim HDB text, such as the quoted passages on APP p.7 or the infographic text on APP p.9.
  - `AUTHORED-FACT`: a policy fact you wrote yourself, not yet verified against the source.
  - `PROJECT-DECISION`: a design choice.

  Policy facts in the approach doc are marked "unverified" until checked against a frozen source. Examples are "HFE valid 9 months", "12-month assessment ending 2 months before" and "≤10 flats waiver".
- **Anonymity:** no hiring organisation, role, collaborator handle or hackathon branding appears anywhere. The assessment is called "the assessment brief".

### Files

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `INDEX.md` | Purpose, the status and provenance legend, the instruction hierarchy (APP p.1), a file map, and a summary of contradictions and open questions linking to their entries |
| `01_problem_and_scope.md` | Final idea, problem statement, research question, intended narrative, problem-validation stance and the to-do "own research" list. Also the existing-chatbot gap (APP p.2 screenshot, described in text without vendor branding), the theme fit, the **MVP scope table (verbatim structure, APPROVED)**, Core/Limited/Context-only/Exclude semantics, the scope-expansion rule, and the two missing-information categories (A applicant, B corpus). Ends with the demo archetypes and scope-discipline notes |
| `02_policy_sources.md` | The **source-discovery matrix in full** (all policy areas, main sources, exceptions and linked sources, URLs), labelled "not MVP-scoped". The four Dataset A seed pages, supported policy questions, the discovery path (seed → anchors → linked pages → PDFs/visuals), and **media handling** for PDFs, the 2 infographics and the 2 YouTube videos. Also the visual-resource registry fields and policy nuances flagged for the benchmark, all marked AUTHORED-FACT and unverified |
| `03_data_and_licensing.md` | Datasets A, B and C. The private-corpus vs reviewer-facing-corpus split, the `policy_facts.jsonl` role, the source manifest fields and SHA-256, the passage schema, and the rule-registry YAML example. Also extraction-completeness checks (8 rows), the policy coverage matrix, the redistribution rules, the Copyright Act ss 243–244 note, robots.txt and Terms of Use, and the privacy approach (synthetic profiles). Ends with the README data-section draft (APP p.14–15) and data limitations |
| `04_architecture.md` | The 5-stage flow (APP p.17 diagram rebuilt as text/mermaid), essential capabilities, the coverage gate, the structured missing-information contract (4 fields), the verifier policy (3 outcomes, no silent rewrite, at most one regeneration), and hard rules vs soft guidance. Also the **tech-stack table (PROPOSED)**, the LLM provider table and model-selection scorecard (PROPOSED, provisional, no model selected), and the "avoid agents/frameworks/vector DBs" constraint |
| `05_evaluation.md` | The benchmark structure (48 cases = 6 categories × 8), the label-creation protocol (6 steps), the dev/held-out split, annotation and scoring rules, safeguards, the severity rubric, and the **system configurations (both the 3-config and 4-config versions, see C-02)** with the controlled-variables table. Also **all metric definitions from both metric tables**, the failure-type taxonomy (5 types), verifier evaluation, runtime vs offline evaluation, statistical reporting, and evaluation risks |
| `06_submission_requirements.md` | Mandatory brief requirements (anonymised): README contents, the 150–250-word deployment section, development narrative, 3–5 min demo, AI-usage section and log upload. Also the critical non-compliance indicators, resource rules, model-justification rules, the scoring weights (20/25/30/15/10), the deadline and effort estimate, and your own README preferences (HTML formatting, core story in README, supporting docs). Ends with the `ai_logs/` layout and the draft AI-usage disclosure |
| `requirements_register.md` | One table: `ID · Statement · Status · Source [doc p.N] · Component · Acceptance evidence · Related IDs / conflicts`. Below it, a **Contradictions** table (C-xx) and an **Open questions** table (Q-xx). Below that, a completeness-audit appendix that I'll fill in after writing |

**ID scheme:** `REQ-<AREA>-<NNN>`, using the areas PRB, SCP, SRC, DAT, LIC, PRIV, ARC, VER, EVL, MOD, SUB, DOC and NFR. IDs are never renumbered; superseded ones stay with their status. Each ID cites every page it comes from, for example `[ASM p.2][APP p.29]`.

**Planned components** that requirements map to (names only, nothing gets built):
- `source_acquisition`, `source_manifest`, `policy_facts_kb`, `rule_registry`, `visual_resource_registry`
- `profile_extractor`, `coverage_gate`, `rule_engine`, `retriever`, `generator`, `verifier`, `report_ui`
- `eval_harness`, `benchmark_dataset`, `verifier_claim_set`
- `docker`, `README`, `ai_logs`

**Separate private file** (Git-ignored): `references/private/submission_private_notes.md`. It would hold the collaborator handle, the portal instruction and the organisation name. This follows APP p.31: "retain in private assessment notes".

**`.gitignore`** would cover `references/private/`, `data/private_corpus/`, any extracted-passage or derived-index directories, and `.DS_Store`.

---

## Part 2 — Contradictions found (I'll record these, not resolve them)

| ID | Conflict | Pages |
|---|---|---|
| C-01 | **The product is named "BTOPath"** in the configuration tables, demo archetypes and metrics text, but "BTO Buddy" or "bto-buddy" everywhere else | APP p.3, 21, 24, 25 vs p.1, 17 |
| C-02 | **The system configurations disagree.** One version has 3: A direct LLM, B RAG, C profile + retrieval + verification, with no rules. The other has 4: A, B, C hybrid with rules and no verifier, D hybrid + verifier. "If time is short, prioritise A, C, D" refers to the 4-config version | APP p.3 vs p.25–26 |
| C-03 | **The primary metric sets differ.** One table has factual accuracy, required-rule recall, missing-info recall, unsupported-claim rate and citation *correctness*. The other drops factual accuracy and adds citation *precision*, appropriate abstention and critical-error rate. Separately, critical errors are named the "primary safety metric" | APP p.24 vs p.26, p.25 |
| C-04 | **The knowledge base source differs.** The tech table says "Curated official HTML/text passages". The data section says the reviewer-facing knowledge base is *independently authored* `policy_facts.jsonl` and the HTML stays private | APP p.21 vs p.4, 13–14 |
| C-05 | **The rule registry cites `source_passage_id: hfe_application_001`.** That is a private-corpus passage ID in a different format from `HFE_001`. Reviewers can't resolve it if rules point at private passages rather than public fact IDs | APP p.4–5, 15 |
| C-06 | **The README data text says "four official HDB webpages".** But MVP "Limited" scope includes priority-scheme considerations, and the priority-schemes page isn't among the four. The matrix also lists the seniors page, MOP, the income-ceiling PDF and the employment/income declaration guides | APP p.4, 14 vs p.6–11, 18 |
| C-07 | **The supported-question lists differ.** One is: process, first-timer couples, HFE preparation, missing info, non-selection. The MVP table adds a Limited priority area and a Context-only loan/grant area. Separately, "4–5 policy areas" | APP p.5 vs p.17–18, p.28 |
| C-08 | **Log upload scope:** the brief requires *all* coding-agent session and chat logs. Your notes say "essential" logs, and your disclosure mentions ChatGPT brainstorming, which isn't a coding agent but is a chat | ASM p.4 vs APP p.30–31 |
| C-09 | **Log upload vs anonymity:** the required logs, including *this session*, will contain the organisation name copied from the brief. Uploading them conflicts with the anonymity requirement unless redacted, and redaction must still satisfy "all logs" | ASM p.2 vs p.4 |
| C-10 | **Verifier failure handling has two versions.** One says remove, label as needing review, or regenerate once. The other says flag for review. It's unclear which applies by default | APP p.22 vs p.27 |
| C-11 | The instruction hierarchy says "the most recently approved decision governs", but **no section carries a date or version**, so recency can't be determined | APP p.1 |
| C-12 | **Income assessment** is a benchmark exception (12-month period, months worked). But the MVP table doesn't say whether income-ceiling or income-calculation checks are allowed, and "Context-only topics must not trigger eligibility calculations" | APP p.22 vs p.17–18 |
| C-13 | A minor inconsistency inside the brief: Annex A says "around 21" sketches but lists 15. This has no effect on the project | ASM p.4–5 |

## Part 3 — Decisions I need from you before writing

1. **Approval status.** Only the MVP scope table and project selection are explicitly marked final (APP p.1, 17). My proposed default:
   - Treat your imperative constraints as `APPROVED`. Examples: don't commit HTML, use `data/private_corpus/`, `policy_facts.jsonl` as the canonical KB, verifier must not silently rewrite, coverage gate, 48-case structure, labelling protocol.
   - Treat the tech table, provider ranking, scorecard, Streamlit, configurations, metric tables and statistical tests as `PROPOSED`.

   OK?
2. **"PolicyProof-inspired verification layer"** (APP p.21) isn't explained anywhere. What is PolicyProof? If it's a prior project of yours, the brief's "recycling a past project" disqualification rule (ASM p.4) makes this worth documenting carefully, or dropping.
3. **Will `docs/project_context/` be committed?**
   - If yes: I'll paraphrase the assessment brief rather than reproduce it, and exclude verbatim HDB text. That means no infographic transcription, only short labelled quotes where the wording is policy-critical, such as the fiancé-under-21 and unwed-parent clauses.
   - If no: I can keep fuller copies and Git-ignore the directory.

   I recommend committing it in paraphrased form.
4. **Anonymity details.** I plan to:
   - omit the chatbot vendor branding from the APP p.2 screenshot description;
   - describe the APP p.29–30 problem-validation idea as "past public-sector hackathon projects", without the event name or URL;
   - keep Annex A only as a short note on which sketches are adjacent to this project (#5 benefits matching, #12 email triage, #15 out-of-KB robustness).

   Agree?
5. **C-01 naming:** should the register use "BTO Buddy" throughout and mark BTOPath as `SUPERSEDED`?
6. **C-02 and C-03:** should I record both configuration sets and both metric sets as `PROPOSED`, with no winner chosen? This decision is required before the evaluation plan is frozen.
7. **"Supabase"** is listed as a demo-video tool (APP p.30), but it isn't a recording tool. Should I record it as a likely error?
8. **Unspecified items** that I'll log as `OPEN` unless you have answers:
   - the dev/held-out split ratio, and whether 48 cases is the total or the test set only
   - the size of the verifier claim set
   - the policy period the app states it supports
   - where the visual-resource registry and rule registry files live
   - the `policy_facts.jsonl` schema
   - whether the robots.txt and Terms of Use checks for hdb.gov.sg have been done
   - verification of the Copyright Act ss 243–244 claim
   - the "own research" statistics, which must not be invented

Once you approve, or adjust, items 1–8, I'll create the 8 files, the private notes file and `.gitignore`. Then I'll run a page-by-page source-to-Markdown audit (every APP and ASM page and image against the register) and report omissions, unresolved conflicts and anything still awaiting your approval.

<pasted_content id="6baf">
# Conflict Resolution and Approval to Create Project Context

Before proceeding, I want to resolve the identified contradictions and clarify the authoritative project decisions.

**Treat the decisions below as my approved clarifications**, subject to the mandatory assessment requirements. Preserve the original documents as references, but do not treat superseded approaches as active implementation requirements.

## 1. Approval status and instruction hierarchy

Use these statuses:

- `MANDATORY`: Explicit requirements from the official assessment.
- `APPROVED`: Final project decisions, including the clarifications in this message.
- `PROPOSED`: Technical alternatives or implementation details not yet approved.
- `OPEN`: Questions that genuinely cannot be resolved from the documents or this message.
- `HISTORICAL` / `SUPERSEDED`: Earlier ideas or decisions replaced by approved ones.

The final MVP scope, canonical reviewer-facing knowledge base, hybrid architecture, evaluation safeguards and source-handling restrictions are approved.

The following remain subject to evidence-based technical selection: specific LLM provider/model, retrieval improvements beyond BM25, verifier model choice, statistical tests and implementation optimisations.

**Instruction priority:**

1. Mandatory official assessment requirements.
2. My latest explicit instructions and approved decisions, where compatible with the assessment.
3. The finalised project scope, architecture, data strategy and evaluation methodology.
4. The current approved implementation task.
5. Proposed alternatives and unresolved questions.
6. Historical or superseded brainstorming.

If a material improvement or conflict is identified, explain the current approach, alternative, tradeoffs and assessment implications. Obtain my approval before deviating.

Record the approval date and a decision ID for each newly resolved decision.

## 2. Resolve the identified contradictions

**C-01 — Project naming**

The canonical project name is **BTO Buddy**.

Use:

- Repository and distribution: `bto-buddy`
- Python package: `bto_buddy`
- Application name: BTO Buddy

Mark BTOPath as a superseded working name.

**C-02 — System configurations**

Adopt the four-configuration design:

- A: Direct LLM — applicant profile and question, without retrieval or deterministic policy rules.
- B: RAG — same generation model with retrieved policy evidence.
- C: Hybrid — structured applicant profiling, deterministic rules and RAG.
- D: Hybrid + runtime factual verification.

Use the same underlying generation model, equivalent task instructions and benchmark cases wherever applicable.

For C versus D, reuse identical pre-verification outputs to isolate the effect of verification.

If time is constrained, prioritise A, C and D, documenting why B was omitted.

Mark the earlier three-configuration design as superseded.

**C-03 — Evaluation metrics**

Adopt the following primary metrics:

1. Critical-error rate.
2. Required-rule recall.
3. Missing-information recall.
4. Unsupported-claim rate.
5. Appropriate abstention.

Use citation precision, factual correctness, answer coverage, latency and inference cost as supporting metrics.

Evaluate retrieval independently using recall\@k on labelled queries, and evaluate the runtime verifier separately using independently labelled supported, contradicted and insufficient-evidence claims.

Define all metrics operationally, including denominators, before evaluation. Preserve the critical/major/minor error-severity rubric.

**C-04 — Canonical knowledge base**

The reviewer-facing `data/policy_facts.jsonl` is the canonical runtime, retrieval and primary evaluation knowledge base.

The original HTML snapshots and extracted source-derived passages are stored under `data/private_corpus/` for local source auditing, extraction and completeness validation. They are not reviewer-facing.

Normal application execution and reviewer evaluation must not depend on the private corpus.

**C-05 — Rule references**

The structured rule registry must reference stable, reviewer-accessible fact IDs, which resolve to official source URLs and relevant sections through the source manifest.

Private passage IDs may be retained for provenance but must not be necessary for runtime execution.

**C-06 — Four seed pages versus additional sources**

The four original HDB webpages are **seed sources**, not necessarily the complete approved corpus.

The source-discovery matrix identifies additional candidate sources, including priority schemes, linked FAQs, PDFs and relevant exceptions.

A subsequent prompt in phase 2 will determine the minimum source set required for the MVP. No linked source should be automatically included merely because it appears in the matrix.

Do not claim that the final corpus consists of exactly four pages until source discovery and coverage validation confirm this.

**C-07 — Supported policy scope**

The final MVP scope table is authoritative:

- Core: first-timer couple household composition, broad BTO application requirements, HFE prerequisites/timing/documentation and missing applicant information.
- Limited and source-verified: relevant first-timer/priority considerations and application/non-selection consequences.
- Context only: high-level relationship between HFE, grants and loans.
- Excluded: grant and loan eligibility calculations, detailed financing, ballot probability prediction, post-purchase conditions and comprehensive official eligibility determination.

The supported-question inventory must reflect these distinctions.

**C-08 — AI logs**

The assessment requires all coding-agent session and chat logs, not merely selected or successful sessions.

Replace references to "essential logs" with "complete project-specific coding-agent session and chat logs".

ChatGPT was used for project planning based on my ideas. You do not have to disclose this in the AI-assisted development narrative since only coding-agent logs were requested. Do not automatically include full non-coding brainstorming transcripts.

**C-09 — Logs and anonymity**

Preserve complete substantive coding-agent development history, including this Phase 0 session.

Before submission, audit exported logs for identifying information, credentials, sensitive local paths and restricted source material.

Where necessary, redact only information that genuinely requires protection, preserve the structure and substance of the session, and document redactions transparently.

Do not selectively remove failed sessions or rewrite historical prompts.

If the assessment's completeness and anonymity requirements cannot both be satisfied confidently, flag the conflict for my decision rather than silently omitting logs.

**C-10 — Verification failure handling**

Adopt this default behaviour:

- Supported: display the claim with a verified source reference.
- Contradicted: withhold the unqualified claim and flag the contradiction.
- Insufficient evidence: avoid definitive guidance and identify the evidence gap or need for official confirmation.

Do not silently rewrite unsupported claims.

One controlled regeneration attempt may be considered as an optional improvement, but it is not required for the MVP and must be approved before implementation.

**C-11 — Decision recency**

Create `docs/decisions.md` with decision IDs, approval dates, status, rationale and superseded decisions.

Use the latest explicitly approved decision when resolving conflicts, provided it complies with the assessment.

**C-12 — Income assessment**

Include income/employment information only insofar as it is necessary for HFE preparation, identifying required documents and asking relevant follow-up questions.

Do not implement comprehensive income eligibility calculations, income-ceiling determinations or financing calculations.

Income assessment exceptions may be included in the benchmark only where they are within the approved preparation scope and supported by verified policy evidence.

**C-13 — Assessment brief inconsistency**

Record the Annex A sketch-count discrepancy as a minor source-document inconsistency with no impact on implementation. Do not spend further effort resolving it.

## 3. Clarify the remaining questions

**PolicyProof:** This was an earlier brainstorming concept for evidence-grounded AI factual verification, not an existing implemented project. BTO Buddy is a new implementation that incorporates relevant verification principles.

**Project context documentation:** Commit `docs/project_context/` to the repository after reviewing it for anonymity, copied source content and other restricted information. Use independently authored summaries rather than reproducing substantial copyrighted material.

**Anonymity:** Keep organisation-specific assessment details, collaborator handles and private submission instructions in `references/private/`, excluded from Git. Submission-facing documentation should describe the project as a public-sector AI prototype.

**Supabase:** It is a tool that I may use to annotate my screen recording demo video. Leave it in the document.

**Benchmark split:** Target 48 fictional scenarios in total across six categories, with a development/held-out split that preserves category coverage. Propose the exact split before dataset creation; do not assume that all 48 cases form the held-out test set. Suggest if K-fold cross validation is better suited instead of the same held-out test set.

**Verifier claim set:** Propose an appropriately sized, independently labelled development and evaluation claim set based on the available time and evaluation objectives. Do not fabricate labels.

**Policy period:** Record source retrieval dates and known effective dates. The precise supported policy snapshot period will be finalised after source acquisition and validation.

**Data paths:**

- `data/policy_facts.jsonl`
- `data/policy_rules.yaml`
- `data/visual_resources.json`
- `data/sources_manifest.json`
- `data/source_coverage.csv`
- `data/private_corpus/raw/`
- `data/private_corpus/processed/`

**Policy facts schema:** Propose a minimal typed schema with stable fact IDs, factual statements, applicability conditions, exceptions, source references, temporal metadata and validation status. Finalise it during architecture and corpus design.

**Rights and permissions:** Record the previously identified HDB Terms of Use, robots.txt restrictions and Singapore Copyright Act computational-data-analysis considerations as preliminary findings requiring source verification during phase 2. Do not claim that HDB has granted general redistribution permission.

**Problem-validation research:** Preserve the research questions as optional evidence-gathering tasks. Do not invent statistics about applicant confusion, hotline enquiries or operational benefits.

## 4. Proceed with Phase 0 documentation extraction

You may now create:

- `docs/project_context/INDEX.md`
- `docs/project_context/01_problem_and_scope.md`
- `docs/project_context/02_policy_sources.md`
- `docs/project_context/03_data_and_licensing.md`
- `docs/project_context/04_architecture.md`
- `docs/project_context/05_evaluation.md`
- `docs/project_context/06_submission_requirements.md`
- `docs/project_context/requirements_register.md`
- `docs/decisions.md`
- `references/private/submission_private_notes.md`
- `.gitignore`

Before writing `.gitignore`, ensure it excludes `references/private/`, `data/private_corpus/`, secrets, local environments and caches.

Preserve the complete source-discovery matrix, including source URLs, content structures, linked resources, tables, expandable sections and media types.

Preserve every substantive requirement and its original PDF page reference. Distinguish approved decisions from proposals and unresolved questions.

Do not reproduce substantial HDB webpage text or private assessment content in Git-tracked documentation.

After creating the files:

1. Perform the promised page-by-page and image-by-image completeness audit.
2. Map requirements to their canonical context sections and acceptance evidence.
3. Identify any remaining contradictions, omissions or ambiguous requirements.
4. Report the final files created and their status.
5. Present any unresolved decisions requiring my approval before Phase 1.

Do not implement application functionality, download external policy sources, select the final LLM model, commit or push during this phase.

decision approved here governs, provided it complies with the mandatory assessment
requirements (D-001, D-012).

document, page N; `[DEV 2026-10-28]` = developer clarification given on that date.

[project_context/requirements_register.md](project_context/requirements_register.md).

---

## Instruction priority (D-001)

1. Mandatory assessment requirements.
2. The developer's latest explicit instructions and approved decisions, where compatible with the assessment.
3. The finalised project scope, architecture, data strategy and evaluation methodology.
4. The current approved implementation task.
5. Proposed alternatives and unresolved questions.
6. Historical or superseded brainstorming.

Any material improvement or conflict found later must be raised with:
- the current approach;
- the alternative;
- the trade-offs;
- the assessment implications.

The developer must approve it before any deviation.

This replaces the hierarchy in [APP p.1], which is recorded as superseded in BD-00.

| D-002 | Canonical name **BTO Buddy**. Repo/distribution `bto-buddy`; Python package `bto_buddy`; application name "BTO Buddy". "BTOPath" is a superseded working name | APPROVED | C-01 | One consistent name across code and docs | "BTOPath" [APP p.3, 21, 24, 25] |
| D-003 | Four system configurations: A Direct LLM (profile + question, no retrieval, no rules); B RAG (same model + retrieved evidence); C Hybrid (structured profiling + deterministic rules + RAG); D Hybrid + runtime factual verification. All use the same generation model, equivalent task instructions and the same benchmark cases wherever applicable. C vs D reuses identical pre-verification outputs. If time is short, run A, C and D and document why B was omitted | APPROVED | C-02 | Ablation isolates the effect of each component | 3-configuration design [APP p.3] |
| D-004 | **Primary metrics:** critical-error rate, required-rule recall, missing-information recall, unsupported-claim rate, appropriate abstention. **Supporting metrics:** citation precision, factual correctness, answer coverage, latency, inference cost. **Component evaluations:** retrieval recall@k on labelled queries; runtime verifier on independently labelled supported/contradicted/insufficient claims. All metrics are defined operationally, with denominators, before evaluation. The critical/major/minor severity rubric is kept | APPROVED | C-03 | Puts safety first and makes each component measurable | Primary/secondary list [APP p.24]; table [APP p.26] (definitions kept) |
| D-005 | `data/policy_facts.jsonl` is the canonical runtime, retrieval and primary-evaluation KB. HTML snapshots and source-derived passages live under `data/private_corpus/`, for local auditing, extraction and completeness validation only. Running the app and the reviewer evaluation must not depend on the private corpus | APPROVED | C-04 | Reproducible on a clean machine and rights-compliant | Tech-table row "Knowledge base: curated official HTML/text passages" [APP p.21] |
| D-006 | The rule registry references stable, reviewer-accessible **fact IDs**. These resolve to official URLs and sections through the source manifest. Private passage IDs may be kept for provenance but are never needed at runtime | APPROVED | C-05 | Reviewers can resolve every rule citation | `source_passage_id` in the rule example [APP p.15] |

Nothing is included just because it appears in the source-discovery matrix. Don't claim a four-page corpus until coverage validation confirms it | APPROVED | C-06 | Coverage is decided by evidence | "four official HDB webpages" wording [APP p.14] |

Core: first-timer couple household composition, broad BTO application requirements, HFE prerequisites/timing/documentation, missing applicant information. Ballot prediction and comprehensive determination are added to the exclusions | Supported-question list [APP p.5] |

Redact only what genuinely needs protection, keep the structure and substance, and document every redaction in `ai_logs/redactions.md`. Never remove failed sessions or rewrite prompts. | D-021 | Record source retrieval dates and known effective dates. The supported policy snapshot period is set after source acquisition and validation | APPROVED (period OPEN) | Proposal Q8 | — | — |

# 01 — Problem and Scope

The status and provenance legend is in [INDEX.md](INDEX.md#legend). Requirement IDs are
defined in [requirements_register.md](requirements_register.md).

## 1. Project identity

| Item | Value | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Project | **BTO Buddy**: a pre-application preparation assistant for Build-To-Order (BTO) flat applicants | APPROVED | [APP p.1], D-002 |
| Repository / package / app | `bto-buddy` / `bto_buddy` / "BTO Buddy" | APPROVED | D-002 |
| "BTOPath" | Earlier working name, found in some tables and figures | SUPERSEDED | [APP p.3, 21, 24, 25] |
| "PolicyProof" | Earlier brainstorming concept for evidence-grounded factual verification. Never implemented. BTO Buddy borrows its verification principles only | HISTORICAL | [APP p.21], D-015 |
| Stakeholder | Citizen group (prospective BTO applicants) | APPROVED | [APP p.29], REQ-PRB-001 |
| Assessment theme | Retrieval & knowledge (primary). The verification layer also touches "generation with guardrails" | APPROVED (primary), inference (secondary) | [APP p.29], [ASM p.1] |

## 2. Final revised idea — REQ-PRB-010 (APPROVED) [APP p.1–2]

- BTO applicants face a **sequence of decisions**:
  - applicant eligibility;
  - household composition;
  - income;
  - HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter requirements;
  - priority schemes;
  - application consequences.
- The problem is **not** that official information is missing. Applicants struggle to work
  out which rules apply to *their* circumstances, and what information they still need
  before they proceed.
- Official tools already exist: HFE assessments, eligibility guidance and application
  information. BTO Buddy adds a **pre-application preparation layer** that helps applicants:
  - understand the relevant published rules;
  - identify missing information;
  - prepare questions before they use the official application process.
- **Differentiation:** transparency and preparation. BTO Buddy does not replace the
  authoritative assessment.

### 2.1 Observed gap in existing channels [APP p.1–2] (developer observation)

**The HDB website's virtual assistant.**
- A screenshot in the project approach shows a test query: a first-timer with four previous
  unsuccessful BTO attempts asks whether they have an advantage at the next attempt.
- The assistant replied that it did not understand and asked the user to rephrase. It then
  listed three generic links:
  - a First-Timer (Parents & Married Couples) priority-scheme page on an external
    government services directory;
  - "Application for a New Flat";
  - "Modes of Sale".
- The user is left to read through the linked pages themselves.

**The website itself.**
- Pages link to anchors on the same page, to other portal pages, or to external resources
  such as PDFs and other sites.
- Information relevant to one user group is scattered across pages, and irrelevant content
  is still shown, so important clauses are easy to miss unless every expandable section is
  opened.
- Some content exists only in infographics (images) or in videos hosted on YouTube.
- An applicant may qualify for several schemes without realising it. The site works more as
  an **information dump** than as applicant-centred guidance.

**Effect on users:** a generic, non-personalised experience that causes fatigue.

### 2.2 Potential downstream benefit — HYPOTHESIS ONLY (REQ-PRB-015) [APP p.2]
Better-prepared citizens *could* reduce HDB operational load: fewer hotline enquiries and
fewer ineligible applications to process. This needs future user testing to validate and
quantify, and must not be claimed as a result.

## 3. Problem statement — REQ-PRB-011 (APPROVED) [APP p.3]
> BTO applicants must navigate multiple interdependent eligibility and application rules.
> While authoritative guidance exists, translating these rules into personalised, actionable
> preparation steps can require substantial manual interpretation. BTO Buddy aims to reduce
> that burden while keeping official sources and human verification central to the process.

*(This is the developer's own text; "bto-buddy" is normalised to "BTO Buddy" per D-002.)*

## 4. Research question — REQ-PRB-012 (APPROVED) [APP p.3]
> Can a hybrid AI assistant combining structured applicant profiling, authoritative policy
> retrieval and evidence verification provide more reliable BTO pre-application guidance than
> a conventional LLM assistant?

**Intended narrative [APP p.3]:**
1. Identify a real public-service information challenge.
2. Build an assistant that turns complex published requirements into personalised
   preparation guidance.
3. Evaluate whether structured reasoning and evidence verification make it more reliable
   than simpler approaches.

## 5. Problem validation — REQ-PRB-013, REQ-PRB-014 [APP p.3, 29–30], D-025

- **APPROVED stance:**
  - Policy *complexity* can be substantiated from official documentation: multiple
    eligibility pathways, detailed income rules, HFE requirements, application consequences
    and exceptions.
  - The *frequency* of applicant confusion needs separate supporting evidence.
  - **Never invent** statistics about call-centre volume, citizen frustration or operational
    benefit.
- **Optional research tasks (OPEN, not started):**
  - volume of BTO applications;
  - demographics of BTO applicants;
  - general sentiment about BTO applications, including applicant confidence and the share
    of young applicants who feel confused;
  - volume of avoidable hotline enquiries.
- **Optional evidence route (PROPOSED) [APP p.29–30]:** given the short timeframe, cite
  findings from *past public-sector hackathon projects* as predecessors. Use them only where
  they are publicly documented, and cite them accurately.

## 6. MVP scope — REQ-SCP-001 (APPROVED, authoritative) [APP p.17–18], D-008

This table is the approved functional scope. Earlier source-discovery findings, ideas and
proposed enhancements **do not** expand it automatically (REQ-SCP-007).

| Policy area | Tier | Source |
|---|---|---|
| First-timer couple household composition | **Core** | [APP p.17] |
| Broad BTO application requirements | **Core** | [APP p.18] |
| HFE prerequisites, timing and documentation | **Core** | [APP p.18] |
| Missing applicant information | **Core** | [APP p.18] |
| Relevant first-timer and priority considerations | **Limited, source-verified** | [APP p.18] |
| Application and non-selection consequences | **Limited, source-verified** | [APP p.18] |
| High-level HFE / loan / grant explanations (relationship only) | **Context only** | [APP p.18] |
| Grant and loan eligibility calculations | **Excluded** | [APP p.18] |
| Detailed affordability and financing | **Excluded** | [APP p.18] |
| Post-purchase conditions | **Excluded** | [APP p.18] |
| Ballot probability prediction | **Excluded** | D-008 (new 2026-10-28) |
| Comprehensive official eligibility determination | **Excluded** | D-008 (new 2026-10-28) |
| Videos explaining existing written guidance | **Excluded from the core retrieval corpus.** Optional contextual links only, when the topics "Step 1: Check Preliminary HFE" or "Step 2: Apply for HFE Letter" are relevant to the query | [APP p.18] |

### 6.1 Tier semantics (APPROVED) [APP p.17]

| Tier | Rule | ID |
|---|---|---|
| Core | Must be implemented **and** evaluated | REQ-SCP-002 |
| Limited | May be implemented only where authoritative evidence and testable requirements exist | REQ-SCP-003 |
| Context only | May be explained or linked. Must **not** trigger independent eligibility calculations | REQ-SCP-004 |
| Excluded | Handled by the **coverage gate**, with redirection to the official source | REQ-SCP-005 |

Any scope expansion needs explicit approval **and** an update to the evaluation plan
(REQ-SCP-006).

### 6.2 HFE boundary statement — REQ-SCP-008 (APPROVED) [APP p.18]

**BTO Buddy does:**
- explain how the HFE process relates to flat-purchase eligibility, CPF housing grants and
  HDB housing-loan eligibility;
- identify the relevant preparation requirements;
- direct applicants to authoritative sources.

**BTO Buddy does not:**
- calculate grant amounts;
- determine loan eligibility or financing amounts;
- compare loan products;
- replace the official HFE assessment.

Questions that need these determinations are redirected to the relevant official services.

### 6.3 Income and employment boundary — REQ-SCP-010 (APPROVED) D-013
- Income and employment details are used **only** for HFE preparation: identifying required
  documents and asking relevant follow-up questions.
- No comprehensive income-eligibility calculation, no income-ceiling determination and no
  financing calculation.
- Income-assessment exceptions enter the benchmark only if they are within preparation scope
  and backed by verified evidence.

### 6.4 Supported-question inventory — DRAFT (PROPOSED; finalised in Phase 2 per D-007/D-008)

The original list [APP p.5] is SUPERSEDED by D-008. It read: high-level BTO process and
requirements, first-timer couples, HFE preparation, missing information, non-selection
consequences. The draft below is derived from the approved tiers.

| Tier | Example question types |
|---|---|
| Core | "We're a first-timer couple. What do we need to prepare before applying for a BTO?"; "Do we need an HFE letter, and when should we apply?"; "What documents does HFE need for my employment situation?"; "Who can be listed as applicant/occupier?" |
| Limited | "Are there first-timer or priority considerations that may be relevant to us?" (identify and link only); "What happens if we don't select a flat when invited?" |
| Context only | "How does the HFE letter relate to grants and loans?" (explanation only, no amounts) |
| Excluded → gate | "How much grant will we get?"; "Can we afford a 4-room?"; "What are our chances in the ballot?"; "Can we rent out after MOP?"; "Confirm that we are eligible." |

**OPEN (Q-05):** whether non-couple household types count as out-of-scope, or as "Limited"
recognition with redirection. Examples are multi-generation, orphaned siblings,
non-resident family members, seniors and unwed parents (see [02](02_policy_sources.md)).

## 7. Missing information: two distinct categories — REQ-SCP-013 (APPROVED) [APP p.18–19]

These must be kept separate in the architecture, the benchmark and the documentation.

| Category | Meaning | Examples | Required behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Missing applicant information** | The applicant hasn't given a detail needed to identify the relevant preparation requirements | One partner's citizenship status is unknown; HFE application/approval status is unspecified; prior flat ownership or application is not stated; employment information is needed but not supplied | Ask a targeted follow-up, or name the information to prepare. **Never assume missing values** |
| **B. Missing policy information in the corpus** | The frozen KB lacks enough authoritative evidence to answer reliably | A linked FAQ with an exception was never included; an accordion condition wasn't extracted; an infographic has a step absent from the text; the policy changed after capture; the passage exists but retrieval missed it | Don't invent an answer. Flag insufficient evidence or unsupported coverage and direct the user to the official source |

The failure sub-types of category B are listed in [05 §8](05_evaluation.md#8-failure-type-taxonomy-category-b-root-cause).
The runtime contract is in [04 §3](04_architecture.md#3-structured-missing-information-contract).

## 8. Demo archetypes — REQ-SCP-014 [APP p.20–21]

These are for the 3–5 minute video. They are **not** the evaluation dataset and can still be
refined.

| Scenario | Description | Capability shown |
|---|---|---|
| A — Straightforward applicant | A fictional first-time couple gives a complete profile. BTO Buddy identifies the relevant preparation requirements and links official sources | Straightforward guidance |
| B — Missing information | A couple gives incomplete employment or household information. BTO Buddy asks targeted follow-ups instead of making an unsupported determination | Missing-information handling |
| C — Policy misconception | An applicant assumes something incorrect about application consequences. BTO Buddy retrieves the official guidance, explains the distinction and flags uncertainty where needed | Verification layer |

- **APPROVED constraint:** the demo examples must represent actual system behaviour. Don't
  pick only unusually easy cases that hide known failure modes.
- The original text called Scenario C valuable for the "PolicyProof-inspired" verification
  layer. That label is HISTORICAL (D-015).

## 9. Scope discipline and non-claims (APPROVED) [APP p.28]

- **REQ-SCP-012:** a small system that handles **4–5 policy areas** accurately, with a
  rigorous baseline comparison, beats a broad, unreliable assistant.
- **REQ-SCP-011:** never claim comprehensive coverage of all current and historical BTO
  policies. Rules vary by application date, flat classification, applicant category and
  policy changes. A statement can be correct for one sales exercise and wrong for another.

## 10. Positioning against the brief's illustrative sketches [ASM p.5–6]

The brief offers optional, anonymised problem sketches, and choosing any of them is not
required. The nearest ones are:
- profile-driven benefits matching;
- citizen-enquiry triage with escalation;
- out-of-knowledge-base robustness for RAG ("I do not know" vs confabulation).

BTO Buddy is an independent problem formulation, not a selected sketch.

# 03 — Data, Licensing and Privacy

The legend is in [INDEX.md](INDEX.md#legend).

## 1. Data assets overview

| Asset | Path (D-022) | Git | Role | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raw HDB HTML snapshots, PDFs | `data/private_corpus/raw/` | **Ignored** | Local provenance, extraction, completeness validation | APPROVED (BD-03, D-005) |
| Extracted source-derived passages; any index built from them | `data/private_corpus/processed/` | **Ignored** | Local auditing only | APPROVED |
| Source manifest | `data/sources_manifest.json` | Tracked | URLs, titles, timestamps, hashes, extraction method | APPROVED |
| Source coverage matrix | `data/source_coverage.csv` | Tracked | Policy/extraction coverage evidence | APPROVED (path); format PROPOSED |
| **Policy facts KB (canonical)** | `data/policy_facts.jsonl` | Tracked | Runtime, BM25 retrieval, primary evaluation | APPROVED (D-005); schema PROPOSED (D-023) |
| Structured rule registry | `data/policy_rules.yaml` | Tracked | Deterministic checks | APPROVED (path); content after Phase 2 |
| Visual-resource registry | `data/visual_resources.json` | Tracked | Infographic/video links and display conditions | APPROVED (path) |
| Evaluation scenarios (Dataset C) | path OPEN (Q-10) | Tracked | Benchmark | APPROVED (design); not yet created |
| Verifier claim set | path OPEN (Q-10) | Tracked | Verifier evaluation | APPROVED (D-020); size PROPOSED |
| Saved predictions and run metadata | path OPEN (Q-10) | Tracked | Reproducible offline scoring | APPROVED (REQ-DAT-018) |

## 2. Dataset A — source acquisition and reviewer-facing KB [APP p.4–5, 11–14]

### 2.1 Two corpora (APPROVED, D-005)
- **Private source corpus:**
  - the original HDB HTML pages and approved linked resources;
  - kept locally for provenance, extraction and policy-completeness validation;
  - full snapshots and extracted copied-text passages are **excluded from Git**
    (REQ-LIC-010, REQ-LIC-011).
- **Reviewer-facing canonical KB:** `data/policy_facts.jsonl`, which holds
  **independently authored, source-attributed factual policy representations**. Each has
  passed manual validation and rights review (REQ-DAT-010).
- The application, BM25 index, Docker deployment and primary evaluation **all use the
  reviewer-facing corpus** (REQ-DAT-011).
- The private corpus is **not** needed for normal execution or reviewer evaluation
  (REQ-DAT-012).
- The matrix, snapshots and extraction reports support building and auditing the authored
  facts. They don't expand the MVP (REQ-SCP-007).

### 2.2 Same interface, no transfer of claims (APPROVED) [APP p.13], REQ-DAT-013
- Both corpora should be usable through the **same retrieval interface**.
- Document any coverage differences between them.
- **Never claim that results on one corpus apply to the other.**
- **OPEN (Q-11):** is any experiment planned on the private corpus? If not, the
  same-interface requirement only needs to hold structurally.

### 2.3 Source manifest — REQ-SRC-002 (APPROVED) [APP p.4, 14]
Required fields per source:
- URL;
- document title;
- access timestamp;
- source section;
- extraction method;
- **SHA-256 hash** of the snapshot, to show it didn't change between experiments;
- relevant policy scope [APP p.14].

### 2.4 Private passage record (APPROVED structure, private corpus only) [APP p.4–5]
- **REQ-SRC-003:** each passage keeps enough context to avoid misreading an exception. For
  example, a condition must not be separated from the heading that names its applicant group.
- Example fields from the source document:

  ```json
  {
    "passage_id": "HFE_001",
    "source_id": "HFE_APPLICATION",
    "section": "Application Requirements",
    "source_url": "https://www.hdb.gov.sg/...",
    "anchor": "#application-requirements",
    "content_type": "html",
    "retrieved_at": "2026-10-26",
    "policy_effective_date": null,
    "text": "Locally extracted source content",
    "review_status": "pending"
  }
  ```

- `text` holds copied source content, so these records live only under
  `data/private_corpus/processed/`.

### 2.5 `policy_facts.jsonl` schema — PROPOSED (D-023; finalise in architecture/corpus design)

One JSON object per line. Typed with Pydantic in code.

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `fact_id` | str, stable, e.g. `HFE-VALIDITY-001` | Referenced by rules, labels and citations. Never reused |
| `statement` | str | **Independently authored** factual paraphrase. No substantial copied text |
| `topic` | enum (e.g. `household`, `hfe`, `income_docs`, `application`, `non_selection`, `priority`) | Retrieval facets and coverage gate |
| `scope_tier` | enum `core` / `limited` / `context` | Links to the MVP tier |
| `applies_to` | object of conditions (e.g. `{"household_type": "first_timer_couple"}`) | Applicability |
| `exceptions` | list of `{description, fact_id?}` | Keeps exceptions attached |
| `source` | `{source_id, url, section, anchor}` | Resolves through `sources_manifest.json` |
| `private_passage_ids` | list[str] (optional) | Provenance only; never needed at runtime (D-006) |
| `retrieved_at` | date | Temporal metadata |
| `effective_from` / `effective_to` | date or null; plus `effective_date_note` | Known effective dates and ambiguity |
| `validation` | `{status: draft/verified/rejected, method, validated_at, notes}` | Manual validation |
| `rights_review` | `{status: pending/cleared, notes}` | Rights review before it is tracked |
| `kb_version` | str | Corpus versioning |

### 2.6 Extraction (APPROVED) [APP p.11]
- **REQ-SRC-006:**
  - capture **only explicitly approved webpages**, by manual rendered-DOM extraction or
    controlled browser automation, subject to documented access and usage permissions;
  - preserve expanded informational sections;
  - **never** follow links automatically or interact with transactional services;
  - no automated discovery or unrestricted crawling [APP p.14].
- **REQ-SRC-007:** extract and normalise headings, paragraphs, tables, lists, links and
  document metadata.
- Media rules are in [02 §4](02_policy_sources.md#4-media-handling-decisions-approved-app-p1112-18).

### 2.7 Validate completeness and freeze — REQ-SRC-012, REQ-SRC-013 (APPROVED) [APP p.12–13]

Freezing involves a coverage matrix, missing exceptions, source hashes and manual review.

**(a) Extraction completeness.** Did the pipeline capture what the approved sources display?

| Check | Method |
|---|---|
| Accordion coverage | Compare discovered controls with successfully expanded controls |
| Section coverage | Compare visible page headings with extracted headings |

- **REQ-SRC-007:** extract and normalise headings, paragraphs, tables, lists, links and
  document metadata.
- Media rules are in [02 §4](02_policy_sources.md#4-media-handling-decisions-approved-app-p1112-18).

### 2.7 Validate completeness and freeze — REQ-SRC-012, REQ-SRC-013 (APPROVED) [APP p.12–13]

Freezing involves a coverage matrix, missing exceptions, source hashes and manual review.

**(a) Extraction completeness.** Did the pipeline capture what the approved sources display?

| Check | Method |
|---|---|
| Accordion coverage | Compare discovered controls with successfully expanded controls |
| Section coverage | Compare visible page headings with extracted headings |
| Link coverage | Classify relevant links as included, excluded or pending review |
| Table preservation | Check row/column values against the rendered source |
| Policy exception coverage | Manually inspect exceptions and conditional wording |
| Source traceability | Verify that passage IDs map to real URLs and sections |
| Temporal validity | Record known effective dates and unresolved date ambiguity |
| Duplicate passages | Detect duplicates without discarding distinct exceptions |

**(b) Policy coverage completeness.** Does the captured information contain the
requirements and exceptions the supported scenarios need?
- Every supported rule has **at least one verified authoritative source**.
- Every important exception has been checked.
- Example: a "declining flat selection" case is **not** covered just because the corpus has
  a general first-timer paragraph. The relevant exceptions must be represented too.
- Stored in `data/source_coverage.csv`.

### 2.8 Temporal validity — REQ-SRC-015 (APPROVED) [APP p.28], D-021
- Every reference document records:
  - source URL;
  - retrieval date;
  - effective date where available;
  - applicable scope.
- The application **states the policy period it supports**. That period is set after
  acquisition and validation (OPEN until Phase 2).

## 3. Dataset B — structured policy rule registry [APP p.15], REQ-DAT-014, D-006

- A small machine-readable registry, so policy logic isn't buried in prompts.
- **Encode only rules whose conditions are explicit and reliably established.** Discretionary
  decisions are never forced into binary rules (for example, unwed-parent cases are assessed
  holistically).
- **Benefits:**
  - deterministic, unit-testable checks;
  - clear separation of policy facts from model explanations;
  - a defensible architecture for a consequential public-service domain.
- **Example** (original APP p.15, updated per D-006):

  ```yaml
  rule_id: HFE_REQUIRED
  scope: new_flat_application
  condition:
    requires_valid_hfe: true
  outcome:
    preparation_step: "Obtain a valid HFE letter"
  source_fact_id: HFE-REQUIRED-001     # D-006: reviewer-accessible fact ID
  # source_passage_id: hfe_application_001   # SUPERSEDED (private passage ID; may be kept as provenance)
  requires_human_review: false
  ```

## 4. Dataset C — independently labelled evaluation scenarios [APP p.15–16]

The full design is in [05_evaluation.md](05_evaluation.md#3-benchmark-dataset-c).

- **REQ-DAT-016:** Dataset C is kept **separate from the knowledge corpus and from the
  runtime verifier**.
- **REQ-DAT-017:** profiles are fictional and use synthetic names. **Real applicant records
  are never used.**
  - Reason: real records are sensitive and hard to access.
  - Synthetic profiles suit controlled rule testing and edge-case coverage.
- **Defence of synthetic data** (needed by REQ-DAT-002):
  - scenarios are *policy-derived* from verified rules and vary one or two factors at a
    time, including boundary conditions;
  - labels are assigned manually against official rules, never invented by an LLM.

## 5. Licensing, access and permissions

### 5.1 Preliminary findings — to verify in Phase 2 (D-024)
- **REQ-LIC-013:** HDB website materials are subject to HDB's published **Terms of Use** and
  copyright.
  - Singapore's **Copyright Act 2021, ss 243–244**, gives a conditional exception for
    *computational data analysis*, covering certain copying and retention, subject to
    lawful-access, purpose and sharing restrictions.
  - This is a *preliminary* reading. The statutory text and the Terms of Use must be checked.
- **REQ-LIC-014:** **robots.txt** compliance [ASM p.2] for every host:
  - `www.hdb.gov.sg`;
  - `file.go.gov.sg`;
  - `www.mynicehome.gov.sg`;
  - (YouTube: links only).

  Status: **not yet checked**.
- **REQ-LIC-012:** **never claim HDB has granted a general redistribution licence.**
- **REQ-LIC-016:** a script may support lawful acquisition. Re-downloading current pages
  can't rebuild a historical frozen snapshot, so hashes and capture dates must be recorded.

### 5.2 Redistribution rules (APPROVED) [APP p.13–14]
- **Git-ignored:**
  - full HDB HTML files;
  - extracted passages containing substantial original text;
  - source-derived indexes containing such text.

  These stay ignored unless redistribution permission is established.
- **May be tracked, subject to content and rights review:**
  - independently authored factual representations;
  - source URLs and metadata;
  - rule definitions and evaluation labels;
  - processing scripts.
- The three-way distinction to document:
  1. A private source snapshot, for local extraction and analysis.
  2. A reviewer-accessible, independently authored policy KB.
  3. A frozen evaluation dataset of fictional scenarios with independently checked labels.
- **REQ-LIC-015:** before submission, review **all tracked data** for copyright, privacy
  and credential exposure.
- **REQ-LIC-017 (D-016):** project-context docs use authored summaries, never substantial
  copyrighted text.

## 6. Privacy — REQ-PRIV-001, REQ-PRIV-010
- **No real personal data:** all profiles are fictional [APP p.16].
- **Deployment limitation [APP p.28]:** free-tier API data-handling terms may not suit
  personal information in a real deployment that ingests applicant data. This feeds the
  model-selection justification (REQ-MOD-001) and the deployment-risk section (REQ-DOC-002).
- **The app never touches transactional services** such as Singpass or the HDB Flat Portal
  (REQ-SRC-006).

## 7. Reproducibility — REQ-DAT-018, REQ-DAT-021, REQ-DAT-022 (APPROVED) [APP p.13–15]
- **Reviewer path:**
  - The repo includes the rights-reviewed `policy_facts.jsonl`, the rules, the source
    metadata and the evaluation datasets.
  - Reviewers build the retrieval index and run the Dockerised app **without downloading HDB
    pages or rebuilding the private corpus**.
- **Developer scripts:** source-capture and extraction scripts are optional and documented.
  They are **not** dependencies of startup or of primary evaluation.
- **Clean-machine test:** a clean-machine Docker test must prove the reviewer-facing
  configuration works (REQ-NFR-001).
- **Live API runs vary,** so each run records:
  - model identifiers;
  - prompt versions;
  - inference settings;
  - corpus versions;
  - **saved predictions**.

  Reproducible offline scoring is reported separately from new live inference.

## 8. README data-section draft (PROPOSED wording, APP p.14–15)

The draft paragraphs in the source cover: data sources, data acquisition (hybrid,
scope-controlled, manual approval, optional browser automation for expandable sections, no
crawling), source provenance (manifest), licensing and access, data handling and
redistribution, reproducibility and limitations.

The draft must be revised before use:
- It says the prototype uses **"four official HDB webpages"**. That is SUPERSEDED by D-007;
  report the final source count after Phase 2.
- It must reflect D-005 (canonical KB) and D-024 (preliminary rights findings).

## 9. Data limitations (APPROVED, for README) [APP p.15, 28]
- Policy content reflects the retrieved versions and may miss later changes.
- No live retrieval. The static KB and rule registry need **manual updates after each policy
  change**, which makes maintenance effort high.
- Synthetic profiles support controlled testing. They **can't establish** how often real
  applicants misunderstand rules, or how the assistant performs on real enquiries.
- The prototype gives informational preparation guidance. It doesn't replace the official
  eligibility assessment.
- **Representativeness (REQ-DAT-003):** state what the data covers and doesn't cover. That
  means the MVP tiers, the household types and the policy period.

Structured extraction and validation
Pydantic schema, missing fields, contradictions"] --> G G{"Coverage gate
within supported policy areas?"} G -- no --> OOS["Out-of-scope response
+ official-source redirection"] G -- yes --> S2A & S2B S2A["2A. Rule engine
explicit policy conditions & preparation requirements"] --> S3 S2B["2B. Evidence retrieval
BM25 over curated policy facts"] --> S3 S3["3. Evidence-grounded response generation
structured explanation, citations, missing-information checklist"] --> S4 S4["4. Claim-level verification
Supported / Contradicted / Insufficient evidence"] --> S5 S5["5. Applicant-facing preparation report
verified guidance, flagged uncertainty, official source links"] ``` **Retrieval corpus note.** The diagram says "BM25 over curated policy passages". Placing it after profile extraction and before retrieval is the author's reading, PROPOSED (Q-12). | Stage | Planned component | Status | |---|---|---| | 1 | `profile_extractor` (LLM → Pydantic) plus deterministic field validation | APPROVED design | | Gate | `coverage_gate` | APPROVED | | 2A | `rule_engine` reading `data/policy_rules.yaml` | APPROVED | | 2B | `retriever` (BM25) | APPROVED. Embeddings PROPOSED, conditional (§6) | | 3 | `generator` (one selected LLM) | APPROVED design; model OPEN | | 4 | `verifier` | APPROVED design; method/model OPEN | | 5 | `report_ui` | APPROVED design; UI framework PROPOSED | ## 3. Structured missing-information contract — REQ-ARC-005 (APPROVED, BD-06) [APP p.20] Every response object carries these four fields: | Field | Meaning | Behaviour | |---|---|---| | `missing_profile_fields` | Applicant attributes needed for personalised guidance but not provided | Targeted clarification where appropriate. **Never assume values** (REQ-ARC-013) | | `evidence_gaps` | Missing or insufficient authoritative policy evidence | **Prevents unsupported definitive conclusions** | | `profile_conflicts` | Contradictory applicant information | Ask for clarification | | `out_of_scope_reasons` | Questions or scenarios outside the MVP | Coverage-gate response and redirection | **REQ-ARC-014:** missing evidence must **never** be read as proof that a requirement doesn't exist. ## 4. Representation principles (APPROVED) [APP p.22, 28] - **REQ-ARC-006:** represent policies as conditions, exceptions, effective dates and source references in structured metadata, never just as paragraphs. - **REQ-ARC-007:** use typed objects throughout (retrieved evidence, applicable rules, missing fields, verification results). Never pass unstructured text between modules. This enables component-level error analysis. - **REQ-ARC-008: hard rules vs soft guidance.** - Clearly documented requirements are checked deterministically. Example: a valid HFE letter is needed. - Complex interpretations stay **evidence-linked explanations that need official confirmation**. - Document which decisions are deterministic and which need retrieval or human review. - **REQ-ARC-009:** LLM answers link to the actual HDB webpages as sources [APP p.13]. ## 5. Runtime verification (APPROVED) [APP p.22, 26–28], D-011 | Outcome | Displayed behaviour (D-011) | |---|---| | **Supported** | Show the claim with a verified source reference | | **Contradicted** | Withhold the unqualified claim and flag the contradiction | | **Insufficient evidence** | No definitive guidance. Add embeddings **only if** they demonstrably improve recall on the benchmark (retrieval recall@k, [05 §5](05_evaluation.md)). **REQ-ARC-011:** use one generation model and no unnecessary orchestration. ### 6.2 LLM API provider comparison — PROPOSED, **preliminary** [APP p.22] > The rankings are provisional and may be stale. Label them as preliminary, not as verified > current recommendations (REQ-MOD-010). **No model is selected in Phase 0.** | Provider | Advantages | Limitations | Assessment (provisional) | |---|---|---|---| | Google AI Studio | Free-tier access to selected Gemini models, structured outputs, Python SDK | Rate limits and free-tier data-use considerations | First to test | | GroqCloud | Fast inference, accessible open-weight models, free-plan limits | Model-dependent capabilities and request limits | Strong alternative | | OpenRouter | Multiple models through one interface | Provider-specific privacy and availability | Useful fallback | | Ollama | Local inference, control over input data | Hardware-dependent performance | Only if privacy demands it | Other permitted resources [ASM p.4][APP p.26, 29]: - **LLM APIs:** Hugging Face Inference Providers, Cerebras, Together AI. - **Local inference:** llama.cpp, LM Studio. - **GPU:** Colab, Kaggle Notebooks, Lightning AI. - **Weights and data:** Hugging Face, Kaggle. ### 6.3 Model-selection scorecard — PROPOSED [APP p.22–23] | Criterion | Weight | |---|---| | Policy reasoning accuracy | 35% | | Structured output reliability | 25% | | Handling uncertainty | 20% | | Latency | 10% | | Estimated cost | 10% | **REQ-MOD-001 (MANDATORY):** - Justify the final choice on operational grounds: data sensitivity, latency, task fit, fine-tuning needs, cost-at-scale economics. - **Never** on "free, cool, had it lying around" [ASM p.4]. - Local vs API doesn't matter in itself. **Gap.** The scorecard has no data-privacy criterion, although the brief names privacy as a valid ground. See Q-13.
