# 05 — Evaluation

The legend is in [INDEX.md](INDEX.md#legend).

**MANDATORY context [ASM p.2–3]:**
- Select and justify a specific evaluation methodology, with the rationale in the README.
- **Soundness outranks the size of the results.**
- Evaluation and effectiveness carry the largest scoring weight (30%).
- Novelty counts only together with effectiveness.
- Be honest about limitations (REQ-EVL-001, REQ-EVL-002).

**Chosen methodology (APPROVED):** a **controlled benchmark with an ablation-style
comparison** of system configurations. The runtime verifier and the retriever are also
evaluated as separate components.

## 1. System configurations — REQ-EVL-010 (APPROVED, D-003) [APP p.25–26]

| System | What it includes | Question answered |
|---|---|---|
| A — Direct LLM | Applicant profile + question → model response. No retrieval, no deterministic rules | How well does a simple assistant perform? |
| B — RAG | Retrieved policy evidence → model response (same model) | Does grounding improve reliability? |
| C — Hybrid | Structured profiling + deterministic rules + RAG | Do structured checks improve guidance? |
| D — Hybrid + verifier | Full BTO Buddy pipeline | Does verification reduce exposed errors? |

### Controlled variables [APP p.25, image 2]

| Dimension | A | B | C | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Same generation model | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Same applicant input | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Same supported policy scope | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Pretrained knowledge | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Retrieved policy facts | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Structured profile extraction | No separate module | No separate module | Yes | Yes |
| Deterministic policy rules | No | No | Yes | Yes |
| Claim verification | No | No | No | Yes |

- **REQ-EVL-011:** use the same generation model, equivalent task instructions and the same
  benchmark cases. All configurations are scored against **the same authoritative reference
  labels and the same policy version**.
- **REQ-EVL-012 (D-003):** C vs D **reuses identical pre-verification outputs**, so the
  difference isolates the verifier.
- **REQ-EVL-013:** if time is short, run **A, C and D** and document why B was omitted. That
  still gives a baseline, the core intervention and the verification ablation.
- **Purpose:** show *why* the added engineering complexity is justified, rather than assuming
  a more elaborate architecture is better [APP p.3].
- **Verification ablation [APP p.24, 26]:** enabled vs disabled on identical cases. This
  tests measurable value and also exposes false alarms, latency and cost.
- **SUPERSEDED [APP p.3]:** the three-configuration design (A baseline, B RAG,
  C "BTOPath" = profile + retrieval + verification). Its evaluated aspects were factual
  correctness, required-rule coverage, unsupported-claim rate, missing-information
  detection, abstention and latency. All of these are carried into §4.

## 2. Two separate evaluation activities (APPROVED) [APP p.27, image]

| Evaluation type | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Runtime verification | Checks generated claims against retrieved evidence before they are shown |
| Independent offline evaluation | Measures whether the application **and its verifier** are actually correct |

**REQ-EVL-029:** the offline benchmark has independently reviewed labels. **The runtime
verifier's judgements are never ground truth** [APP p.25, 27].

## 3. Benchmark (Dataset C) — REQ-EVL-014 (APPROVED, D-019) [APP p.15–16]

### 3.1 Structure: 48 fictional cases in total, 6 categories × 8

| Category | Cases | What it tests |
|---|---|---|
| Standard preparation | 8 | Correct applicable requirements |
| Missing information | 8 | Appropriate follow-up questions |
| Policy exceptions | 8 | Handling nuanced conditions |
| Misconceptions | 8 | Correcting inaccurate assumptions |
| Conflicting information | 8 | Detecting contradictory profile details |
| Out-of-scope | 8 | Abstaining appropriately |

- **REQ-EVL-032 [APP p.27]:** expand the three demo archetypes into many independently
  labelled cases covering different profiles, rules and edge conditions.
- Include conflicting-information and out-of-scope cases even if the video doesn't show them.

### 3.2 Label-creation protocol — REQ-EVL-016..019 (APPROVED) [APP p.16]
1. **Extract policy requirements first.** Build a rule inventory with source references.
2. **Design scenario templates.** Vary one or two meaningful factors at a time, including
   boundary conditions.
   - Use **policy-derived scenarios**. Never ask an LLM to invent eligibility labels.
   - Independently check the expected guidance against official rules (REQ-EVL-017).
3. **Write fictional profiles** with synthetic names. Never use real records.
4. **Assign expected outcomes manually.** Record:
   - applicable rules;
   - required follow-up information;
   - prohibited conclusions;
   - supporting passages (now fact IDs, D-006).
5. **Review labels independently of the model** (REQ-EVL-018).
   - Ideally a second reviewer checks a sample.
   - If no second reviewer is available, run a separate source-based audit and **disclose
     that the labels were author-validated**.
6. **Freeze the held-out set** (REQ-EVL-019). Its labels never change after final
   predictions are inspected, except to correct documented annotation errors.

**From the same page [APP p.16, image]:**
- Use development cases for prompt and architecture refinement.
- Keep a separate held-out set for the final comparisons.
- Balance cases across categories where possible.
- **Report performance by category** (REQ-EVL-035).

### 3.3 Dev/held-out split — PROPOSED (needs approval before dataset creation, D-019)

**Recommendation: a fixed, stratified, group-aware split. 18 development / 30 held-out.**

| Category | Dev | Held-out |
|---|---|---|
| Each of the 6 categories | 3 | 5 |
| **Total** | **18** | **30** |

- **Group-aware:** cases from the same scenario template or near-duplicate family all go to
  the *same* side, as REQ-EVL-022 requires. If grouping makes 3/5 impossible in a category,
  the split moves by at most one case and the change is documented.
- **Why not K-fold:**
  1. K-fold suits estimating a *trained* model's variance. No model is trained here. The
     "fitting" is manual prompt and architecture iteration, which can't be repeated
     independently per fold without leaking every case into development.
  2. The approved safeguards require dev and held-out cases to be **separated before prompt
     optimisation**, and the held-out set to be **frozen and untouched**. K-fold conflicts
     with both.
  3. Each run costs live API calls under free-tier limits.
- **Uncertainty with 30 held-out cases:** handle it with paired per-case comparisons and
  bootstrap intervals (§7), not with folds.
- **Trade-off:** 30 held-out cases give wide intervals. That is acceptable for a controlled
  benchmark if it's reported honestly (REQ-EVL-031).
- **Alternative (not recommended):** 24/24. This gives more test power but leaves only 4 dev
  cases per category, which is too few to iterate on prompts per category.

## 4. Metrics — REQ-EVL-024..026 (APPROVED hierarchy, D-004)

All definitions must be **operational, with denominators, and frozen before evaluation**
(REQ-EVL-026). The definitions below come from [APP p.24, 26]. Where the source is silent,
the operationalisation is marked PROPOSED.

### 4.1 Primary metrics

| # | Metric | Definition | Denominator / unit | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Critical-error rate** | Cases with ≥1 *critical* error (severity rubric §4.3) ÷ evaluated cases. Major errors reported separately | Cases | [APP p.25–26] |
| 2 | **Required-rule recall** | Correct required rules identified ÷ all applicable reference rules | Rule instances, pooled over cases (PROPOSED: also report per-case macro mean) | [APP p.24, 26] |
| 3 | **Missing-information recall** | Correctly identified essential missing fields ÷ all reference missing fields | Field instances, pooled (PROPOSED: macro too) | [APP p.24, 26] |
| 4 | **Unsupported-claim rate** | Unsupported factual claims ÷ all *checkable* factual claims, measured at claim level | Claims. **PROPOSED:** claim segmentation and the "checkable" criterion need a written annotation guide (Q-14) | [APP p.24, 26] |
| 5 | **Appropriate abstention** | Correct abstentions ÷ cases whose reference label requires abstention or official confirmation. Scored **only** on such cases | Cases requiring abstention. **PROPOSED:** also report the *over-abstention* rate on answerable cases, so abstaining everywhere can't game the metric | [APP p.24, 26] |

**Priority [APP p.26]:** critical-error rate and required-rule recall matter most. A concise
but incomplete answer can be less dangerous than one that confidently tells an ineligible
applicant to proceed.

### 4.2 Supporting metrics

| Metric | Definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Citation precision | Correctly supported cited claims ÷ all claims with citations. "Supported" means the cited evidence **substantively** supports the claim | [APP p.24, 26] |
| Factual correctness | Proportion of independently labelled factual claims answered correctly | [APP p.24] ("factual accuracy") |
| Answer coverage | **Not defined in the sources → OPEN (Q-15).** PROPOSED: answerable cases given substantive (non-abstaining) guidance ÷ answerable cases | D-004 |
| Latency | **PROPOSED:** median and p95 end-to-end seconds per configuration | [APP p.3, 24] |
| Inference cost | **PROPOSED:** recorded tokens × published price, per case and per configuration (or $0 plus a compute note for local) | [APP p.24] |
| Human-review burden (verification flags) | Listed as secondary in [APP p.24] but **not in D-004 → OPEN (Q-16)** | [APP p.24] |

### 4.3 Critical-error severity rubric — REQ-EVL-023 (APPROVED) [APP p.25]

| Severity | Definition | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Critical** | A materially misleading preparation or eligibility conclusion | Stating eligibility definitively without sufficient evidence |
| **Major** | Missing an important applicable requirement | Omitting an essential HFE prerequisite |
| **Minor** | Non-consequential incompleteness or a presentation issue | Repeating a preparation step |

The primary safety metric counts **critical** errors. **Major** errors are reported separately.

### 4.4 Reference labels and scoring rules (APPROVED, define and freeze before final evaluation) [APP p.24]

**Reference labels — REQ-EVL-020.** Each case records:
- applicable policy rule IDs;
- required missing applicant fields;
- expected response behaviour;
- prohibited or materially misleading conclusions;
- supporting authoritative source references (fact IDs);
- whether the scenario is answerable within the supported corpus.

**Scoring rules — REQ-EVL-021:**
- Required-rule recall is measured against the reference applicable-rule set.
- Missing-information recall is measured against the reference missing fields.
- The unsupported-claim rate is measured at the factual-claim level.
- Citation correctness requires the cited evidence to substantively support the claim.
- Critical errors follow the predefined severity rubric.
- Abstention is scored only where the label requires abstention or official confirmation.

**Scorer — OPEN (Q-17).** Neither source document says whether claim-level judgements
(supported, critical) are made by the author manually, by an LLM-as-judge validated against
manual labels, or both.

### 4.5 Evaluation safeguards — REQ-EVL-022 (APPROVED) [APP p.24–25]
- Separate development and held-out cases **before** prompt optimisation.
- Never split near-duplicate scenarios across dev and test.
- The runtime verifier is never the sole source of ground truth.
- Independently review and document ambiguous labels.
- Report final test results with **raw counts and denominators**.
- Disclose any change made after inspecting held-out results. The affected test set must
  not then be presented as untouched.

## 5. Retrieval evaluation — REQ-EVL-027 (APPROVED, D-004) [APP p.20]
- Measure **recall@k** on labelled queries, where each query has its gold fact IDs. This
  isolates *retrieval failure* (category B).
- The value of k and the labelled-query set are PROPOSED for Phase 2/3. A natural source is
  the benchmark cases' supporting fact IDs.
- The same metric decides whether embeddings are added (REQ-ARC-010).

## 6. Verifier evaluation — REQ-EVL-028 (APPROVED, D-004, D-020) [APP p.27]

**Measures:**
- precision and recall for detecting **contradicted** claims;
- precision and recall for detecting **insufficient-evidence** claims;
- **false-alarm rate** on supported claims;
- **false-approval rate**: how often the verifier wrongly approves a claim;
- added latency and inference cost.
- *Only if relevant:* macro-F1, contradiction recall, false-alarm rate and evidence-retrieval
  accuracy.

**Rationale:** don't assume a verifier is accurate just because it produces classifications.

### 6.1 Claim set — PROPOSED size (needs approval; labels never fabricated, D-020)

| Split | Supported | Contradicted | Insufficient | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Development | 5 | 5 | 5 | 15 |
| Evaluation | 15 | 15 | 15 | 45 |
| **Total** | 20 | 20 | 20 | **60** |

**Construction** (author-labelled against verified facts; disclosed as author-validated):

| Label | How the claims are built |
|---|---|
| Supported | Faithful paraphrases of verified facts |
| Contradicted | Single-attribute perturbations of verified facts: a changed number, period, applicant group, or a dropped exception. The "dropped exception" case targets the risk in [APP p.27] |
| Insufficient | Plausible claims on topics the KB deliberately doesn't cover, or claims that go beyond what the evidence states |

- Each claim is paired with the evidence passed to the verifier.
- **Balanced classes** keep the per-class precision and recall interpretable.
- **Fallback if time is short:** 36 claims (6 dev / 30 eval, i.e. 2/2/2 and 10/10/10). Report
  that intervals will be wide.

## 7. Statistical reporting (APPROVED principle; tests PROPOSED per D-001) [APP p.27]
- With about 48 cases (30 held-out under §3.3), **don't over-interpret small percentage
  differences**.
- Report raw counts alongside percentages, and use paired comparisons (REQ-EVL-030).
- **Options:**
  - paired bootstrap confidence intervals on system differences;
  - McNemar's test for binary case-level success, with an **exact** method for small samples.
- **REQ-EVL-031:** the README states this is a **controlled benchmark, not evidence of
  population-level effectiveness**.

## 8. Failure-type taxonomy (category B root cause) — REQ-EVL-033 (APPROVED) [APP p.19–20]

| Failure type | Meaning | How to test |
|---|---|---|
| Source coverage gap | Relevant document never included | Manual source coverage matrix |
| Extraction gap | Content exists in the source but wasn't extracted | HTML/visual completeness audit |
| Retrieval failure | Content is in the index but wasn't retrieved | Retrieval recall@k |
| Temporal gap | Corpus doesn't cover the applicable policy period | Effective-date checks |
| Evidence insufficiency | Available material can't establish the answer | Abstention and verifier evaluation |

This separation enables meaningful **root-cause error analysis**.

## 9. Policy exceptions the benchmark should test — REQ-EVL-034 [APP p.21–22]

The candidate exceptions are listed in [02 §5](02_policy_sources.md#5-policy-nuances-flagged-for-structured-reasoning-app-p2122):
- HFE validity and timing;
- income assessment (only within D-013);
- household composition (applicants / occupiers / core family nucleus; fiancé(e) under 21);
- non-selection consequences and waivers.

Each must be **verified against frozen sources** before it is labelled.

Additional candidate (author observation): the VR-1 30-day Step-2 window, as an
extraction-gap test ([02 Row 2](02_policy_sources.md)).

## 10. Evaluation risks and what would strengthen the evaluation [APP p.27–28]
- **Automated verification is not automatically trustworthy:**
  - two LLMs can share a misunderstanding;
  - a verifier can approve a claim from a passage that omits an exception.

  Mitigation: independent labels and a separate verifier evaluation.
- **Strong signals named in the approach:**
  - a well-designed benchmark;
  - an error taxonomy;
  - a baseline comparison;
  - evidence that the system catches subtle policy inaccuracies more reliably than a simpler
    approach;
  - evidence that hybrid rules + RAG **reduces unsupported eligibility recommendations**
    compared with a general-purpose chatbot.
- **Demo honesty:** demo examples must represent real behaviour (REQ-SCP-014).

# 06 — Submission Requirements

> collaborator handle and submission-portal details are kept privately (D-017) and

## 1. Overall task — MANDATORY [ASM p.1]
- Pick a problem relevant to Singapore public-sector stakeholders: an agency, a ministry or
  a citizen group (REQ-PRB-001).
- Build an AI-powered prototype, evaluate it comprehensively, and deliver a **Dockerised
  solution** with professional documentation (REQ-SUB-002).
- **AI must be in the core functionality** (REQ-PRB-002).
- **Themes:**
  - unstructured → structured;
  - retrieval & knowledge;
  - generation with guardrails;
  - agents & workflows.

  Any one theme, a combination, or an alternative is acceptable.
- Classification, detection, retrieval, multimodal and agentic methods are all acceptable.
- **The brief's stated intent:** assess problem identification, scoping and technical
  judgement in using AI tools, especially judging viability and validating outputs
  rigorously.

## 2. Deliverables — MANDATORY [ASM p.2]

| ID | Requirement | Planned evidence |
|---|---|---|

| REQ-PRB-002 | **Significant** AI integration, not just an API call inside a standard web app | Architecture section plus ablation results (A–D) |

- "Can the dataset be uploaded here?" [APP p.30] → resolved by D-005 and §5.2 of
  [03](03_data_and_licensing.md). Authored facts and labels are tracked; HDB snapshots are not.

## 9. Ordering and format constraints to remember
- The **coding-agent section goes at the end** of the README (REQ-SUB-009).
- The **demo URL goes in the README** (REQ-SUB-003).
- The deployment section is **150–250 words** (REQ-DOC-002).
- **REQ-DOC-010 / REQ-DOC-011 tension (author observation):** GitHub sanitises some HTML
  (scripts, styles, some attributes are stripped). Mermaid diagrams render in Markdown
  fences but not inside raw HTML blocks. Plan the README format with this in mind.

# BTO Buddy — Project Context Index

This is a structured, traceable knowledge base built from the project's two private planning
sources:
- the **assessment brief** (`[ASM p.N]`);
- the **project-approach document** (`[APP p.N]`).

Both PDFs are kept locally and are Git-ignored. This documentation is independently
authored: it paraphrases requirements and policy content rather than reproducing them.

**Phase:** 0 (context building).
**Created:** 2026-10-28.
**Code, models or datasets:** none have been implemented, selected or created.

## Files

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [01_problem_and_scope.md](01_problem_and_scope.md) | Final idea, problem statement, research question, problem validation, **MVP scope**, HFE/income boundaries, supported-question draft, missing-information categories, demo archetypes |
| [02_policy_sources.md](02_policy_sources.md) | Seed sources, discovery method, **complete source-discovery matrix**, infographic/video registry candidates, **media-handling decisions**, policy nuances to verify |
| [03_data_and_licensing.md](03_data_and_licensing.md) | Datasets A/B/C, private vs reviewer-facing corpora, manifest, schemas, completeness checks, licensing/robots/copyright, privacy, reproducibility, limitations |
| [04_architecture.md](04_architecture.md) | Pipeline, coverage gate, missing-information contract, representation principles, verifier behaviour, proposed stack, provider comparison, model scorecard |
| [05_evaluation.md](05_evaluation.md) | Configurations A–D, **benchmark structure**, label protocol, proposed split, **metric definitions**, severity rubric, retrieval and verifier evaluation, statistics, failure taxonomy |
| [06_submission_requirements.md](06_submission_requirements.md) | Mandatory deliverables, scoring dimensions, non-compliance indicators, resources, AI-log rules, README requirements |
| [requirements_register.md](requirements_register.md) | **All requirement IDs** with source pages, components and acceptance evidence; contradictions; open questions; completeness audit |
| [../decisions.md](../decisions.md) | Decision log (D-001…D-025, BD-00…BD-09) and the instruction priority |

## Legend

**Status**

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `MANDATORY` | Explicit requirement in the assessment brief |
| `APPROVED` | Final project decision (in the project approach as final, or ratified/added in [decisions.md](../decisions.md)) |
| `PROPOSED` | Technical alternative or implementation detail not yet approved |
| `OPEN` | Cannot be resolved from the sources or decisions; needs a developer answer |
| `HISTORICAL` / `SUPERSEDED` | Earlier idea or decision replaced by an approved one. Kept for traceability, **not** an active requirement |

**Provenance**

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `COPIED-SOURCE` | The project-approach PDF quoted HDB text verbatim at this point. The quotation is **not** reproduced in tracked files |
| `AUTHORED-FACT (unverified)` | Independently paraphrased policy statement. It must be verified against a frozen source before it enters `data/policy_facts.jsonl` |
| `PROJECT-DECISION` | Design choice by the developer (the default for non-policy content) |
| *Author observation* | Point raised while building this knowledge base, not stated in either source |

## Instruction priority (D-001)
1. Mandatory assessment requirements.
2. The developer's latest explicit instructions and approved decisions.
3. Finalised scope, architecture, data strategy and evaluation methodology.
4. The current approved implementation task.
5. Proposed alternatives and open questions.
6. Historical or superseded brainstorming.

## Current open items
- **Contradictions still open:** C-14 (URL mismatch in the matrix), C-15 to C-17 (metric
  and scorecard gaps).
- **Questions:** Q-05 to Q-24.
- **Execution risk:** C-09 / Q-19 (log anonymity).

All are listed in [requirements_register.md §2–3](requirements_register.md#2-contradictions).

**Files** (all new, untracked):

| File | Status |
|---|---|
| [.gitignore](.gitignore) | Excludes `references/private/`, `data/private_corpus/`, secrets, local environments, caches and OS files. `git check-ignore` confirms both PDFs, the private notes and the private corpus are excluded |

| [docs/decisions.md](docs/decisions.md) | Your 25 decisions (D-001 to D-025, dated 2026-10-28), plus BD-00 to BD-09: decisions already stated as final in the approach doc and now ratified. Superseded items are listed with what replaced them |
| [INDEX.md](docs/project_context/INDEX.md) | Legend, instruction priority, file map |
| [01_problem_and_scope.md](docs/project_context/01_problem_and_scope.md) | Problem, research question, MVP scope (including the new exclusions), HFE and income boundaries, draft question inventory, missing-information categories A and B, demo scenarios |
| [02_policy_sources.md](docs/project_context/02_policy_sources.md) | The full source-discovery matrix (5 rows, every URL, expandable sections, tables, PDFs, the 2 infographics, the 2 videos) and the media-handling rules |
| [03_data_and_licensing.md](docs/project_context/03_data_and_licensing.md) | Datasets A, B and C, the two corpora, the manifest, the proposed `policy_facts` schema, the 8 completeness checks, rights findings, reproducibility |
| [04_architecture.md](docs/project_context/04_architecture.md) | The pipeline as a mermaid diagram, the missing-information contract, how verifier results are shown, the proposed stack, provider table and scorecard |
| [05_evaluation.md](docs/project_context/05_evaluation.md) | Configurations A–D, the benchmark, the label protocol, metric definitions with denominators, severity rubric, retrieval and verifier evaluation, statistics |
| [06_submission_requirements.md](docs/project_context/06_submission_requirements.md) | Mandatory requirements in paraphrase, scoring weights, non-compliance indicators, AI-log rules, your README requirements |
| [requirements_register.md](docs/project_context/requirements_register.md) | 150 requirement IDs, each with source pages, the context section, a planned component and acceptance evidence. Also contradictions C-01 to C-17, open questions Q-05 to Q-24, and the page-by-page audit |

**Audit results**
- **Coverage:** every page of both PDFs is mapped to a section and IDs (register §4). That includes all 11 embedded images, re-read at 300 dpi.
- **Deliberate omissions (§4.3):**
  - the verbatim HDB quotes and infographic text, which are now paraphrased and marked "unverified";
  - the text of the brief's example problem sketches;
  - organisation-identifying details, now in the private notes;
  - the chatbot screenshot, now described in text.
- **IDs and links:** every requirement ID used in the docs exists in the register, and every internal link resolves (I fixed 3 broken anchors).
- **Anonymity:** a search of the tracked files for the organisation, role, handle, hackathon and vendor terms found nothing.
- **Copied text:** no 10-word passage from the brief or the HDB quotes appears except URLs, a short list of tool names, and the brief's short list of valid model-justification grounds. None of it is copied prose.

**New contradictions I couldn't resolve**
- **C-14:** in the matrix, the "BTO application process" row names the "Application for a New Flat" page, but its URL is actually the HFE page's (`APP p.10–11`).
- **C-15:** "human-review burden" was a secondary metric in the approach doc but isn't in your new metric list.
- **C-16:** "answer coverage" has no definition in either document.
- **C-17:** the model scorecard has no data-privacy criterion, even though the brief names privacy as a valid reason for choosing a model.

**Decisions needed before Phase 1**
1. **Q-20:** benchmark split. I propose a fixed split of 18 development and 30 held-out cases: 3 and 5 per category, with near-duplicate scenarios kept on the same side.
   - I recommend against K-fold. Nothing is trained, so prompt iteration on every fold would leak cases into development, and it breaks the "freeze held-out before optimising" safeguard.
2. **Q-21:** verifier claim set of 60 (15 dev, 45 eval, equal numbers of supported, contradicted and insufficient), or 36 if time is short.
3. **Q-22:** the `policy_facts` schema in 03 §2.5.
4. **Q-23:** the stack: Streamlit, Pydantic, Pandas and scikit-learn.
5. **Q-12:** place the coverage gate after profile extraction and before retrieval?
6. **Q-10:** file paths for the benchmark, claim set, retrieval test queries and saved predictions.
7. **Q-15, Q-16, Q-17:** define "answer coverage", decide whether to keep human-review burden, and decide who scores claim-level judgements (you manually, an LLM judge checked against your labels, or both).

## 7. Implementation layout — PROPOSED (Phase 1, 2026-10-28; needs approval before code)

### 7.1 Package modules (`src/bto_buddy/`)

| Module | Responsibility | Requirements | LLM? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `contracts.py` | All Pydantic models passed between stages (§7.2). The single source of the typed interfaces | REQ-ARC-005, REQ-ARC-007 | No |
| `knowledge/facts.py` | Load and validate `policy_facts.jsonl` and `sources_manifest.json`; resolve fact ID → URL/section | REQ-DAT-010, REQ-DAT-015, REQ-ARC-009 | No |
| `knowledge/rules.py` | Load `policy_rules.yaml`; evaluate explicit rules against a validated profile | REQ-DAT-014, REQ-ARC-008 | No |
| `profile.py` | Extract an `ApplicantProfile` from free text (LLM, structured output), then **deterministically** compute missing fields and conflicts | REQ-ARC-013, REQ-SCP-013 | Extraction only |
| `gate.py` | Coverage gate: map question topics to MVP tiers; emit `out_of_scope_reasons` | REQ-ARC-004, REQ-SCP-005 | No (see 7.3) |
| `retrieval.py` | BM25 over fact statements behind a corpus-agnostic `Retriever` protocol | REQ-ARC-010, REQ-DAT-013 | No |
| `llm.py` | One provider adapter behind a `LLMClient` protocol. Records model ID and settings. Caches responses to saved predictions | REQ-ARC-011, REQ-DAT-018 | — |
| `generation.py` | Evidence-grounded answer → structured claims with fact-ID citations | REQ-ARC-001 | Yes |
| `verification.py` | Claim → supported / contradicted / insufficient, then display policy D-011 | REQ-VER-001..007 | Method OPEN |
| `pipeline.py` | Composes configurations **A–D from one pipeline with stage toggles**, so model and instructions stay identical. D = verify(saved C outputs) | REQ-EVL-010..012 | — |
| `prompts/` | Versioned prompt templates; the version ID is recorded per run | REQ-DAT-018 | — |
| `eval/` | Dataset loaders, scoring (metric spec), retrieval recall@k, verifier metrics, paired statistics | REQ-EVL-* | No (scorer OPEN, Q-17) |
| `app/` | UI (Streamlit, pending Q-23) | REQ-SUB-003 | — |

### 7.2 Core contracts (names and key fields; finalised with the facts schema, Q-22)
- **`ApplicantProfile`:**
  - typed optional fields (citizenship per person, marital/fiancé status, ages, first-timer
    status, prior ownership/applications, HFE status, employment type);
  - `None` means *not provided*, never a default.
- **`ProfileAssessment`:** `profile`, `missing_profile_fields`, `profile_conflicts`.
- **`CoverageDecision`:** `in_scope: bool`, `tiers`, `out_of_scope_reasons`.
- **`PolicyFact`** (mirrors 03 §2.5), **`PolicyRule`**, **`RuleResult`** (`rule_id`,
  `applies`, `preparation_step`, `source_fact_id`, `requires_human_review`).
- **`Evidence`:** `fact_id`, `score`, `rank`.
- **`Claim`:** `text`, `cited_fact_ids`.
- **`VerifiedClaim`:** `claim`, `outcome`, `display_action`.
- **`PreparationReport`:**
  - `guidance`, `claims`, `evidence_gaps`;
  - the four contract fields;
  - `policy_period`, `config_id`, `run_metadata`.

### 7.3 Proposed answers to open architecture questions

**Q-12 — gate placement.**
- The gate runs after profile extraction and before retrieval and generation.
- The extraction call also tags the question with topics from a **closed enum**. The gate maps
  topics to tiers deterministically.
- An empty or out-of-scope tag set, or zero retrieved evidence above a threshold, returns a
  coverage response.
- **Trade-off:** one LLM call does two jobs. The tagging is evaluated through the out-of-scope
  benchmark category.

**Q-10 — paths:**

| Content | Path |
|---|---|
| Scenarios | `data/eval/scenarios.jsonl` |
| Split | `data/eval/split.json` |
| Verifier claims | `data/eval/verifier_claims.jsonl` |
| Retrieval queries | `data/eval/retrieval_queries.jsonl` |
| Run outputs | `results/runs/<run_id>/{run_metadata.json, predictions.jsonl, scores.json}` (tracked, so offline re-scoring is reproducible) |
| Frozen metric spec | `eval/metric_spec.md` |

**Dependencies, each to be justified when added:**

| Dependency | Justification |
|---|---|
| `pyyaml` | Rule registry format (D-022) |
| `rank-bm25` | Small, standard BM25. Alternative: about 40 lines in-house |
| `streamlit` | UI (Q-23) |
| The chosen provider's SDK, or `httpx` | After model selection |
| `pandas` | Results tables. `scikit-learn` only if a metric needs it |

# 04 — Architecture The legend is in [INDEX.md](INDEX.md#legend). > No code exists yet. Component names are **planned** identifiers, used for traceability in > the [requirements register](requirements_register.md). ## 1. Essential capabilities and constraints (APPROVED) [APP p.16–17] **REQ-ARC-001: the three essential capabilities.** 1. Retrieve authoritative policy evidence. 2. Generate profile-specific preparation guidance, including missing information. 3. Verify factual claims and flag unsupported statements. **REQ-ARC-002: constraints.** - Use deterministic Python validation for known structured fields. - **Avoid** autonomous agents, complex orchestration frameworks and unnecessary vector databases (BD-09). **REQ-PRB-002 tension.** The brief needs *significant AI integration*, not "simply an API call within a standard web app" [ASM p.2]. The argument that this design meets that bar rests on: - LLM-based structured profile extraction; - grounded generation; - claim-level verification; - an ablation (A–D) showing each component's measured contribution. The README must make this argument explicitly. ## 2. Pipeline — REQ-ARC-003 (APPROVED, BD-04) [APP p.17, image] Rebuilt from the diagram, with the coverage gate (REQ-ARC-004) placed as specified in [APP p.21]: ```mermaid flowchart TD IN["User question + fictional applicant profile"] --> S1 S1["1. Structured extraction and validation
Pydantic schema, missing fields, contradictions"] --> G G{"Coverage gate
within supported policy areas?"} G -- no --> OOS["Out-of-scope response
+ official-source redirection"] G -- yes --> S2A & S2B S2A["2A. Rule engine
explicit policy conditions & preparation requirements"] --> S3 S2B["2B. Evidence retrieval
BM25 over curated policy facts"] --> S3 S3["3. Evidence-grounded response generation
structured explanation, citations, missing-information checklist"] --> S4 S4["4. Claim-level verification
Supported / Contradicted / Insufficient evidence"] --> S5 S5["5. Applicant-facing preparation report
verified guidance, flagged uncertainty, official source links"] ``` **Retrieval corpus note.** The diagram says "BM25 over curated policy passages". Under D-005, the retrieval corpus is `data/policy_facts.jsonl`. **Coverage-gate placement.** The diagram doesn't place the gate. [APP p.21] says it runs "before generating a response". Placing it after profile extraction and before retrieval is the author's reading, PROPOSED (Q-12). | Stage | Planned component | Status | |---|---|---| | 1 | `profile_extractor` (LLM → Pydantic) plus deterministic field validation | APPROVED design | | Gate | `coverage_gate` | APPROVED | | 2A | `rule_engine` reading `data/policy_rules.yaml` | APPROVED | | 2B | `retriever` (BM25) | APPROVED. Embeddings PROPOSED, conditional (§6) | | 3 | `generator` (one selected LLM) | APPROVED design; model OPEN | | 4 | `verifier` | APPROVED design; method/model OPEN | | 5 | `report_ui` | APPROVED design; UI framework PROPOSED | ## 3. Structured missing-information contract — REQ-ARC-005 (APPROVED, BD-06) [APP p.20] Every response object carries these four fields: | Field | Meaning | Behaviour | |---|---|---| | `missing_profile_fields` | Applicant attributes needed for personalised guidance but not provided | Targeted clarification where appropriate. **Never assume values** (REQ-ARC-013) | | `evidence_gaps` | Missing or insufficient authoritative policy evidence | **Prevents unsupported definitive conclusions** | | `profile_conflicts` | Contradictory applicant information | Ask for clarification | | `out_of_scope_reasons` | Questions or scenarios outside the MVP | Coverage-gate response and redirection | **REQ-ARC-014:** missing evidence must **never** be read as proof that a requirement doesn't exist. ## 4. Representation principles (APPROVED) [APP p.22, 28] - **REQ-ARC-006:** represent policies as conditions, exceptions, effective dates and source references in structured metadata, never just as paragraphs. - **REQ-ARC-007:** use typed objects throughout (retrieved evidence, applicable rules, missing fields, verification results). Never pass unstructured text between modules. This enables component-level error analysis. - **REQ-ARC-008: hard rules vs soft guidance.** - Clearly documented requirements are checked deterministically. Example: a valid HFE letter is needed. - Complex interpretations stay **evidence-linked explanations that need official confirmation**. - Document which decisions are deterministic and which need retrieval or human review. - **REQ-ARC-009:** LLM answers link to the actual HDB webpages as sources [APP p.13]. ## 5. Runtime verification (APPROVED) [APP p.22, 26–28], D-011 | Outcome | Displayed behaviour (D-011) | |---|---| | **Supported** | Show the claim with a verified source reference | | **Contradicted** | Withhold the unqualified claim and flag the contradiction | | **Insufficient evidence** | No definitive guidance. State the evidence gap or the need for official confirmation | - **REQ-VER-003:** never silently rewrite. No unlimited verification loops. - One controlled regeneration is an **optional improvement** and needs approval (REQ-VER-004). - **REQ-VER-005:** keep *contradicted* separate from *not established*. Treating every unsupported claim as false is a methodological error. - **REQ-VER-007:** the verifier must **withhold, correct or clearly flag** to show a reduction in *exposed* errors. If it only labelled claims, its detection ability would be measured separately (D-011 makes it act). - **REQ-VER-006:** don't assume a second LLM verification call is worthwhile. Compare its incremental error detection against its added cost and latency [APP p.21, 26]. - The verifier method and model are OPEN (D-001). - **Risk [APP p.27]:** - an LLM checking an LLM doesn't establish correctness, because both may misread the same rule; - a verifier can approve a claim on the strength of a superficially relevant passage that omits an exception. This is why the verifier is evaluated independently ([05 §6](05_evaluation.md)). ## 6. # BTO Buddy — Project Context Index

This is a structured, traceable knowledge base built from the project's two private planning
sources:
- the **assessment brief** (`[ASM p.N]`);
- the **project-approach document** (`[APP p.N]`).

Both PDFs are kept locally and are Git-ignored. This documentation is independently
authored: it paraphrases requirements and policy content rather than reproducing them.

**Phase:** 0 (context building).
**Created:** 2026-10-28.
**Code, models or datasets:** none have been implemented, selected or created.

## Files

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [01_problem_and_scope.md](01_problem_and_scope.md) | Final idea, problem statement, research question, problem validation, **MVP scope**, HFE/income boundaries, supported-question draft, missing-information categories, demo archetypes |
| [02_policy_sources.md](02_policy_sources.md) | Seed sources, discovery method, **complete source-discovery matrix**, infographic/video registry candidates, **media-handling decisions**, policy nuances to verify |
| [03_data_and_licensing.md](03_data_and_licensing.md) | Datasets A/B/C, private vs reviewer-facing corpora, manifest, schemas, completeness checks, licensing/robots/copyright, privacy, reproducibility, limitations |
| [04_architecture.md](04_architecture.md) | Pipeline, coverage gate, missing-information contract, representation principles, verifier behaviour, proposed stack, provider comparison, model scorecard |
| [05_evaluation.md](05_evaluation.md) | Configurations A–D, **benchmark structure**, label protocol, proposed split, **metric definitions**, severity rubric, retrieval and verifier evaluation, statistics, failure taxonomy |
| [06_submission_requirements.md](06_submission_requirements.md) | Mandatory deliverables, scoring dimensions, non-compliance indicators, resources, AI-log rules, README requirements |
| [requirements_register.md](requirements_register.md) | **All requirement IDs** with source pages, components and acceptance evidence; contradictions; open questions; completeness audit |
| [../decisions.md](../decisions.md) | Decision log (D-001…D-025, BD-00…BD-09) and the instruction priority |

## Legend

**Status**

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `MANDATORY` | Explicit requirement in the assessment brief |
| `APPROVED` | Final project decision (in the project approach as final, or ratified/added in [decisions.md](../decisions.md)) |
| `PROPOSED` | Technical alternative or implementation detail not yet approved |
| `OPEN` | Cannot be resolved from the sources or decisions; needs a developer answer |
| `HISTORICAL` / `SUPERSEDED` | Earlier idea or decision replaced by an approved one. Kept for traceability, **not** an active requirement |

**Provenance**

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `COPIED-SOURCE` | The project-approach PDF quoted HDB text verbatim at this point. The quotation is **not** reproduced in tracked files |
| `AUTHORED-FACT (unverified)` | Independently paraphrased policy statement. It must be verified against a frozen source before it enters `data/policy_facts.jsonl` |
| `PROJECT-DECISION` | Design choice by the developer (the default for non-policy content) |
| *Author observation* | Point raised while building this knowledge base, not stated in either source |

## Instruction priority (D-001)
1. Mandatory assessment requirements.
2. The developer's latest explicit instructions and approved decisions.
3. Finalised scope, architecture, data strategy and evaluation methodology.
4. The current approved implementation task.
5. Proposed alternatives and open questions.
6. Historical or superseded brainstorming.

## Current open items
- **Contradictions still open:** C-14 (URL mismatch in the matrix), C-15 to C-17 (metric
  and scorecard gaps).
- **Questions:** Q-05 to Q-24.
- **Execution risk:** C-09 / Q-19 (log anonymity).

All are listed in [requirements_register.md §2–3](requirements_register.md#2-contradictions).

# Architecture Review — BTO Buddy (pre-implementation) **Status:** PROPOSED for developer review (2026-10-28). It replaces the held draft (D-029). Nothing here is implemented. Items marked **[APPROVAL]** are choices beyond the approved decisions, or interpretations of them. They are listed again in §13. **Inputs:** [01 scope](../project_context/01_problem_and_scope.md), [03 data](../project_context/03_data_and_licensing.md), [04 architecture](../project_context/04_architecture.md), [05 evaluation](../project_context/05_evaluation.md), [register](../project_context/requirements_register.md), [decisions](../decisions.md). --- ## 1. Recommendation in one paragraph Build a **single, linear, typed pipeline** in plain Python. Each request runs a fixed sequence: 1. **one LLM call** extracts the applicant profile and the question topics, with quotes as evidence; 2. **deterministic code** assesses the profile, applies the coverage gate, evaluates rules and retrieves facts with **BM25 over the ~50–150 authored facts**; 3. **one LLM call** generates cited claims; 4. **verification** runs a deterministic layer plus **one batched LLM judgement call**; 5. a **pure function** assembles the report and applies the D-011 display policy. Every stage boundary is a Pydantic model. Configurations A–D are the same pipeline with stages switched off, and all four emit the same output contract. There are no agents, no vector database, no embeddings and no reranker. Each is held back behind a measurable trigger (§4). ## 2. Requirements that shape the design | Driver | IDs | |---|---| | Three capabilities: retrieve, generate profile-specific guidance, verify | REQ-ARC-001 | | Fixed pipeline, deterministic validation, no agents/frameworks/vector DB | REQ-ARC-002, REQ-ARC-003, BD-09 | | Coverage gate before generation | REQ-ARC-004, REQ-SCP-005 | | Four distinct contract fields | REQ-ARC-005, REQ-SCP-013, REQ-ARC-013, REQ-ARC-014 | | Typed objects between modules | REQ-ARC-007 | | Facts KB only at runtime; rules cite fact IDs | REQ-DAT-010..012, REQ-DAT-015 | | Verifier outcomes and display policy | REQ-VER-001..007, D-011 | | Same model, instructions and labels across A–D; C→D reuse | REQ-EVL-010..012 | | Reproducible runs and offline rescoring | REQ-DAT-018, REQ-NFR-001 | | Free tier, operational model justification | REQ-NFR-004, REQ-MOD-001 | ## 3. End-to-end architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD Q["Free-text situation + question"] --> X X["① extract (LLM #1)
ProfileExtraction: fields + quotes + topics"] --> PA PA["② assess_profile (pure)
quote check · conflicts · topic-required missing fields"] --> G G{"③ coverage_gate (pure)
topics → MVP tiers; household type"} G -- "nothing in scope" --> R G -- "in scope (possibly partial)" --> RE & RT RE["④a rule_engine (pure)
RuleResult: applies / not_applicable / cannot_determine"] --> EV RT["④b retrieve (pure)
BM25 top-k within in-scope topics"] --> EV EV["⑤ assemble_evidence (pure)
rule-linked facts ∪ BM25 hits → EvidenceBundle + evidence_gaps"] --> GEN GEN["⑥ generate (LLM #2)
GenerationOutput: claims citing fact IDs"] --> V V["⑦ verify
deterministic checks → batched LLM judge (#3)"] --> R R["⑧ build_report (pure)
D-011 display policy → FinalGuidance"] ``` ### 3.1 Stages | # | Stage | LLM? | Input → Output | Notes | |---|---|---|---|---| | ① | `extract` | Yes | `UserRequest` → `ProfileExtraction` | Structured output. Every non-null field carries a **verbatim quote** from the input. Also tags question topics from a closed enum | | ② | `assess_profile` | No | `ProfileExtraction` → `ProfileAssessment` | **Quote guard:** a field whose quote isn't a substring of the input is discarded and logged as an extraction warning (anti-hallucination). Detects conflicts. Computes missing fields **only for the topics asked about** | | ③ | `coverage_gate` | No | topics + assessment → `CoverageDecision` | Deterministic topic→tier map (D-008). An unsupported household type is out of scope (default for Q-05). Mixed questions continue with the in-scope part | | ④a | `evaluate_rules` | No | profile + rules → `list[RuleResult]` | **Tri-state.** `cannot_determine` lists the missing fields it needs. Rules produce preparation steps and flags, **never eligibility verdicts** | | ④b | `retrieve` | No | query (question + topic terms) → `list[Evidence]` | BM25 restricted to in-scope topic facts; top-k | | ⑤ | `assemble_evidence` | No | rule results + hits → `EvidenceBundle` | Facts cited by applicable rules are **always included**, so recall on required rules doesn't depend on BM25. Raises `evidence_gaps` when an in-scope topic has no evidence | | ⑥ | `generate` | Yes | profile assessment + rules + evidence → `GenerationOutput` | Atomic claims, each citing fact IDs from the bundle only. Missing fields and conflicts are **passed in, not re-derived** | | ⑦ | `verify` | Deterministic + 1 LLM | claims + bundle → `list[VerificationResult]` | **Deterministic layer first** (a hit decides the outcome, no LLM): no citation → insufficient; citation not in bundle → insufficient; contradicts a deterministic rule result → contradicted. Remaining claims go to **one batched entailment judgement** (supported / contradicted / insufficient) | | ⑧ | `build_report` | No | everything → `FinalGuidance` | Applies D-011: supported → shown with source; contradicted → withheld and flagged; insufficient → stated as unconfirmed, with the gap | - **LLM calls per request:** ① + ⑥ + ⑦ = **3** in config D, **2** in C, **1** in A and B. - **Out-of-scope requests stop after ③:** 1 call, and the report is the redirect. ### 3.2 Configurations A–D from one pipeline (REQ-EVL-010..012) | Stage | A Direct LLM | B RAG | C Hybrid | D Hybrid + verifier | |---|---|---|---|---| | ①–③ profile, gate | — (LLM does it inside ⑥) | — | ✓ | ✓ (reused from C) | | ④a rules | — | — | ✓ | ✓ (reused) | | ④b/⑤ retrieval | — | BM25 on raw question | ✓ | ✓ (reused) | | ⑥ generate | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | **C's saved output** | | ⑦ verify | — | — | — | ✓ | | Output contract | `FinalGuidance` | `FinalGuidance` | `FinalGuidance` | `FinalGuidance` | **[APPROVAL A6] Same structured output for every configuration.** - In A and B, the generation prompt asks the LLM itself to list missing fields, conflicts and out-of-scope reasons, in the **same enums** that C and D fill deterministically. - **Why:** - the metrics (missing-information recall, abstention, required-rule recall) can be scored identically and automatically; - "equivalent task instructions" (D-003) holds; - free-text baselines would need manual mapping to the enums for every case. - **Trade-off:** A becomes a *structured-output* direct LLM rather than a chat-style one. That is a stronger, fairer baseline, but slightly less like a "conventional assistant". The README must say so. - **Alternative:** free-text A and B, scored by manual annotation. Slower, and less reproducible. **Single-turn interaction [APPROVAL A8].** Follow-up questions are *outputs*. The user answers by resubmitting with more detail. There is no conversation memory. Benchmark cases are single-turn. ## 4. Approach comparisons ### 4.1 Rules + BM25 pipeline vs agentic vs vector-database designs | Criterion | **Rules + BM25 pipeline (recommended)** | Agentic (tool-calling LLM decides when to retrieve, check rules, ask) | Vector DB RAG (embeddings + Chroma/FAISS/pgvector) | |---|---|---|---| | Task fit | Fixed, known steps; small closed corpus; deterministic hard rules | Suits open-ended tasks with variable steps; this task's steps are fixed | Suits large or paraphrase-heavy corpora; ours is ~100 authored facts | | Evaluability | Each stage has typed I/O and can be scored alone. Clean A–D ablation | Control flow varies per run, so component attribution and ablation get murky | Adds an embedding-model variable to every result | | Determinism and reproducibility | Only 3 LLM calls, all cached | Variable number of calls; loops; harder to cache | Index depends on the embedding model version | | Latency and cost | 3 calls, bounded | Unbounded calls; more tokens per step | +1 embedding call, or a local model | | Safety in a consequential domain | Rules can't be "skipped" by the model | Model may skip a rule check or retrieval | Same as RAG | | Dependencies | pydantic, pyyaml, BM25 lib | Agent framework (forbidden by REQ-ARC-002) | Vector store + embedding stack (torch ≈ 2 GB image, or an API) | | Assessment alignment | Matches the approved design; justifies complexity through ablation | Conflicts with REQ-ARC-002 / BD-09 | "Unnecessary vector databases" are excluded (REQ-ARC-002) | **Verdict:** the rules + BM25 pipeline. Neither alternative gives a testable benefit at this corpus size, and both are excluded by approved decisions. ### 4.2 Retrieval methods | Method | Strength | Weakness for this corpus | Cost | |---|---|---|---| | **BM25 (recommended)** | Exact matching on policy vocabulary (HFE, FT(PMC), "occupier", "core occupier", "nine months"); explainable scores; deterministic; zero model dependency; sub-millisecond on ~100 docs | Lexical mismatch: "fiancée" vs "fiance", "BTO" vs "new flat", colloquial questions | ~0 | | Semantic (dense embeddings) | Paraphrase matching | Weak on acronyms and numbers; needs torch (≈2 GB image, slow cold start) or an embedding API (another provider, data leaves); version drift | Medium | | Hybrid (BM25 + dense, RRF) | Best of both on large, varied corpora | Both dependencies; tuning a fusion weight on ~100 docs overfits the dev set | Medium–high | | Reranking (cross-encoder or LLM) | Precision at top ranks | Precision isn't the bottleneck: rule-linked facts are always included and k can be generous (~8 facts ≈ 600 tokens). An LLM reranker adds a call | Medium–high | **Recommendation: BM25 only**, with three cheap, deterministic mitigations for its known weakness: 1. **A curated `aliases` field on each fact**, indexed with the statement (e.g. "HDB Flat Eligibility", "HFE letter"; "fiance", "fiancée", "fiancé"). **[APPROVAL A2]**, a one-field schema addition to 03 §2.5. 2. **A topic filter:** search only facts whose topic passed the gate. 3. **Rule-linked facts always included** (stage ⑤). **Testable trigger for anything more:** - On the **dev** retrieval queries, if recall@5 falls below 0.90, *and* error analysis attributes the misses to paraphrase rather than coverage gaps, propose dense or hybrid retrieval as a decision, with before/after recall@k. - Otherwise, don't build it. **Alternative considered and not recommended: put the whole KB in the prompt.** At ~100 facts, it fits in context and removes retrieval failure. But it: - removes the explicit evidence set that the verifier and citations depend on; - scales badly; - inflates per-call cost; - turns config B into something other than RAG. **Implementation choice:** `rank-bm25` (small, pure Python, numpy only). The alternative is about 50 lines in-house; recommended only if you prefer zero dependencies. Tokeniser: lowercase, alphanumeric tokens, numbers kept, a small stop-word list, no stemming library. ## 5. Pydantic contracts (proposed; finalised with the Phase 2 facts schema, Q-22) Field names are indicative. Enumerations that depend on verified policy (employment categories, topics) are confirmed in Phase 2. ```python # ---- shared enums ------------------------------------------------------------- class Tier(StrEnum): CORE="core"; LIMITED="limited"; CONTEXT="context"; EXCLUDED="excluded" class Topic(StrEnum): # in scope (tier fixed by D-008) HOUSEHOLD_COMPOSITION="household_composition" # core APPLICATION_REQUIREMENTS="application_requirements" # core HFE_PROCESS="hfe_process" # core (prerequisites, timing, validity) HFE_DOCUMENTS="hfe_documents" # core (incl. income/employment docs, D-013) PRIORITY_CONSIDERATIONS="priority_considerations" # limited NON_SELECTION="non_selection" # limited HFE_GRANT_LOAN_CONTEXT="hfe_grant_loan_context" # context only # excluded (D-008) GRANT_LOAN_CALCULATION="grant_loan_calculation" FINANCING_AFFORDABILITY="financing_affordability" BALLOT_ODDS="ballot_odds" POST_PURCHASE="post_purchase" ELIGIBILITY_DETERMINATION="eligibility_determination" OTHER_HOUSING="other_housing" # resale, rental, EC, etc. UNRELATED="unrelated" TOPIC_TIER: dict[Topic, Tier] # single source of truth for the gate, unit-tested class ProfileField(StrEnum): # addressable fields, for missing/conflict reporting RELATIONSHIP="relationship"; A1_AGE="applicant_1.age"; A2_AGE="applicant_2.age" A1_CITIZENSHIP="applicant_1.citizenship"; A2_CITIZENSHIP="applicant_2.citizenship" A1_PRIOR_HOUSING="applicant_1.prior_flat_or_subsidy"; A2_PRIOR_HOUSING="applicant_2.prior_flat_or_subsidy" A1_EMPLOYMENT="applicant_1.employment"; A2_EMPLOYMENT="applicant_2.employment" HFE_STATUS="hfe_status"; HFE_ISSUE_DATE="hfe_issue_date" PRIVATE_PROPERTY="private_property_interest"; HOUSING_LOAN_INTENT="housing_loan_intent" CHILDREN="children_or_expecting" # ---- request / profile ------------------------------------------------------------ class UserRequest(BaseModel): request_id: str situation_text: str # free text; fictional profiles only (UI warns) question: str class Person(BaseModel): age: int | None = Field(None, ge=0, le=120) citizenship: Literal["SC", "SPR", "non_resident"] | None = None prior_flat_or_subsidy: bool | None = None # drives first-timer status employment: Literal["employed", "self_employed", "not_working", "other"] | None = None # Phase 2 aligns with HFE guide class ApplicantProfile(BaseModel): """None = not provided. Never defaulted (REQ-ARC-013).""" relationship: Literal["married", "engaged", "other"] | None = None applicant_1: Person = Person() applicant_2: Person = Person() hfe_status: Literal["not_started", "preliminary_done", "applied", "issued"] | None = None hfe_issue_date: date | None = None private_property_interest: bool | None = None housing_loan_intent: Literal["hdb", "financial_institution", "undecided"] | None = None children_or_expecting: bool | None = None class FieldQuote(BaseModel): field: ProfileField quote: str # verbatim span from situation_text class StatedContradiction(BaseModel): field: ProfileField quotes: list[str] = Field(min_length=2) class ProfileExtraction(BaseModel): # LLM #1 output (schema-constrained) profile: ApplicantProfile quotes: list[FieldQuote] stated_contradictions: list[StatedContradiction] question_topics: list[Topic] = Field(min_length=1) # ---- the four distinct signals ------------------------------------------------------- class MissingProfileField(BaseModel): field: ProfileField needed_for: list[str] # topic values and/or rule_ids follow_up_question: str # from a static template map (deterministic) class ProfileConflict(BaseModel): fields: list[ProfileField] kind: Literal["stated_contradiction", "logical_inconsistency"] detail: str # e.g. "engaged, but described as spouse" quotes: list[str] clarification_question: str class EvidenceGap(BaseModel): topic: Topic | None claim_id: str | None = None kind: Literal["no_evidence_for_topic", "claim_uncited", "claim_unsupported", "fact_temporally_uncertain"] detail: str official_source_url: str | None = None # where to confirm class OutOfScopeReason(BaseModel): code: Literal["excluded_topic", "unsupported_household_type", "unrecognised_question"] topic: Topic | None = None detail: str redirect_url: str | None = None # official service/page class ProfileAssessment(BaseModel): profile: ApplicantProfile # after quote guard missing_profile_fields: list[MissingProfileField] profile_conflicts: list[ProfileConflict] extraction_warnings: list[str] # dropped unquoted fields, etc. # ---- gate -------------------------------------------------------------------------- class CoverageDecision(BaseModel): status: Literal["in_scope", "partially_in_scope", "out_of_scope"] supported_topics: list[Topic] out_of_scope_reasons: list[OutOfScopeReason] # ---- knowledge, rules, evidence -------------------------------------------------------- class PolicyFact(BaseModel): # per 03 §2.5 (+ aliases, A2); loaded, never LLM-produced fact_id: str; statement: str; topic: Topic; scope_tier: Tier aliases: list[str] = [] applies_to: dict[str, str] = {}; exceptions: list[str] = [] source_id: str; source_url: HttpUrl; section: str retrieved_at: date; effective_from: date | None; effective_to: date | None validation_status: Literal["verified"] # loader rejects anything else at runtime kb_version: str class RuleResult(BaseModel): rule_id: str; rule_version: str status: Literal["applies", "not_applicable", "cannot_determine"] preparation_step: str | None # only when status == "applies" source_fact_ids: list[str] = Field(min_length=1) missing_fields: list[ProfileField] = [] # required when cannot_determine requires_human_review: bool class Evidence(BaseModel): fact_id: str; statement: str; source_url: HttpUrl; section: str origin: Literal["rule", "bm25"] bm25_score: float | None = None; rank: int | None = None class EvidenceBundle(BaseModel): items: list[Evidence] query: str; k: int; kb_version: str evidence_gaps: list[EvidenceGap] # # Architecture Review — BTO Buddy (pre-implementation) **Status:** PROPOSED for developer review (2026-10-28). It replaces the held draft (D-029). Nothing here is implemented. Items marked **[APPROVAL]** are choices beyond the approved decisions, or interpretations of them. They are listed again in §13. **Inputs:** [01 scope](../project_context/01_problem_and_scope.md), [03 data](../project_context/03_data_and_licensing.md), [04 architecture](../project_context/04_architecture.md), [05 evaluation](../project_context/05_evaluation.md), [register](../project_context/requirements_register.md), [decisions](../decisions.md). --- ## 1. Recommendation in one paragraph Build a **single, linear, typed pipeline** in plain Python. Each request runs a fixed sequence: 1. **one LLM call** extracts the applicant profile and the question topics, with quotes as evidence; 2. **deterministic code** assesses the profile, applies the coverage gate, evaluates rules and retrieves facts with **BM25 over the ~50–150 authored facts**; 3. **one LLM call** generates cited claims; 4. **verification** runs a deterministic layer plus **one batched LLM judgement call**; 5. a **pure function** assembles the report and applies the D-011 display policy. Every stage boundary is a Pydantic model. Configurations A–D are the same pipeline with stages switched off, and all four emit the same output contract. There are no agents, no vector database, no embeddings and no reranker. Each is held back behind a measurable trigger (§4). ## 2. Requirements that shape the design | Driver | IDs | |---|---| | Three capabilities: retrieve, generate profile-specific guidance, verify | REQ-ARC-001 | | Fixed pipeline, deterministic validation, no agents/frameworks/vector DB | REQ-ARC-002, REQ-ARC-003, BD-09 | | Coverage gate before generation | REQ-ARC-004, REQ-SCP-005 | | Four distinct contract fields | REQ-ARC-005, REQ-SCP-013, REQ-ARC-013, REQ-ARC-014 | | Typed objects between modules | REQ-ARC-007 | | Facts KB only at runtime; rules cite fact IDs | REQ-DAT-010..012, REQ-DAT-015 | | Verifier outcomes and display policy | REQ-VER-001..007, D-011 | | Same model, instructions and labels across A–D; C→D reuse | REQ-EVL-010..012 | | Reproducible runs and offline rescoring | REQ-DAT-018, REQ-NFR-001 | | Free tier, operational model justification | REQ-NFR-004, REQ-MOD-001 | ## 3. End-to-end architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD Q["Free-text situation + question"] --> X X["① extract (LLM #1)
ProfileExtraction: fields + quotes + topics"] --> PA PA["② assess_profile (pure)
quote check · conflicts · topic-required missing fields"] --> G G{"③ coverage_gate (pure)
topics → MVP tiers; household type"} G -- "nothing in scope" --> R G -- "in scope (possibly partial)" --> RE & RT RE["④a rule_engine (pure)
RuleResult: applies / not_applicable / cannot_determine"] --> EV RT["④b retrieve (pure)
BM25 top-k within in-scope topics"] --> EV EV["⑤ assemble_evidence (pure)
rule-linked facts ∪ BM25 hits → EvidenceBundle + evidence_gaps"] --> GEN GEN["⑥ generate (LLM #2)
GenerationOutput: claims citing fact IDs"] --> V V["⑦ verify
deterministic checks → batched LLM judge (#3)"] --> R R["⑧ build_report (pure)
D-011 display policy → FinalGuidance"] ``` ### 3.1 Stages | # | Stage | LLM? | Input → Output | Notes | |---|---|---|---|---| | ① | `extract` | Yes | `UserRequest` → `ProfileExtraction` | Structured output. Every non-null field carries a **verbatim quote** from the input. Also tags question topics from a closed enum | | ② | `assess_profile` | No | `ProfileExtraction` → `ProfileAssessment` | **Quote guard:** a field whose quote isn't a substring of the input is discarded and logged as an extraction warning (anti-hallucination). Detects conflicts. Computes missing fields **only for the topics asked about** | | ③ | `coverage_gate` | No | topics + assessment → `CoverageDecision` | Deterministic topic→tier map (D-008). An unsupported household type is out of scope (default for Q-05). Mixed questions continue with the in-scope part | | ④a | `evaluate_rules` | No | profile + rules → `list[RuleResult]` | **Tri-state.** `cannot_determine` lists the missing fields it needs. Rules produce preparation steps and flags, **never eligibility verdicts** | | ④b | `retrieve` | No | query (question + topic terms) → `list[Evidence]` | BM25 restricted to in-scope topic facts; top-k | | ⑤ | `assemble_evidence` | No | rule results + hits → `EvidenceBundle` | Facts cited by applicable rules are **always included**, so recall on required rules doesn't depend on BM25. Raises `evidence_gaps` when an in-scope topic has no evidence | | ⑥ | `generate` | Yes | profile assessment + rules + evidence → `GenerationOutput` | Atomic claims, each citing fact IDs from the bundle only. Missing fields and conflicts are **passed in, not re-derived** | | ⑦ | `verify` | Deterministic + 1 LLM | claims + bundle → `list[VerificationResult]` | **Deterministic layer first** (a hit decides the outcome, no LLM): no citation → insufficient; citation not in bundle → insufficient; contradicts a deterministic rule result → contradicted. Remaining claims go to **one batched entailment judgement** (supported / contradicted / insufficient) | | ⑧ | `build_report` | No | everything → `FinalGuidance` | Applies D-011: supported → shown with source; contradicted → withheld and flagged; insufficient → stated as unconfirmed, with the gap | - **LLM calls per request:** ① + ⑥ + ⑦ = **3** in config D, **2** in C, **1** in A and B. - **Out-of-scope requests stop after ③:** 1 call, and the report is the redirect. ### 3.2 Configurations A–D from one pipeline (REQ-EVL-010..012) | Stage | A Direct LLM | B RAG | C Hybrid | D Hybrid + verifier | |---|---|---|---|---| | ①–③ profile, gate | — (LLM does it inside ⑥) | — | ✓ | ✓ (reused from C) | | ④a rules | — | — | ✓ | ✓ (reused) | | ④b/⑤ retrieval | — | BM25 on raw question | ✓ | ✓ (reused) | | ⑥ generate | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | **C's saved output** | | ⑦ verify | — | — | — | ✓ | | Output contract | `FinalGuidance` | `FinalGuidance` | `FinalGuidance` | `FinalGuidance` | **[APPROVAL A6] Same structured output for every configuration.** - In A and B, the generation prompt asks the LLM itself to list missing fields, conflicts and out-of-scope reasons, in the **same enums** that C and D fill deterministically. - **Why:** - the metrics (missing-information recall, abstention, required-rule recall) can be scored identically and automatically; - "equivalent task instructions" (D-003) holds; - free-text baselines would need manual mapping to the enums for every case. - **Trade-off:** A becomes a *structured-output* direct LLM rather than a chat-style one. That is a stronger, fairer baseline, but slightly less like a "conventional assistant". The README must say so. - **Alternative:** free-text A and B, scored by manual annotation. Slower, and less reproducible. **Single-turn interaction [APPROVAL A8].** Follow-up questions are *outputs*. The user answers by resubmitting with more detail. There is no conversation memory. Benchmark cases are single-turn. ## 4. Approach comparisons ### 4.1 Rules + BM25 pipeline vs agentic vs vector-database designs | Criterion | **Rules + BM25 pipeline (recommended)** | Agentic (tool-calling LLM decides when to retrieve, check rules, ask) | Vector DB RAG (embeddings + Chroma/FAISS/pgvector) | |---|---|---|---| | Task fit | Fixed, known steps; small closed corpus; deterministic hard rules | Suits open-ended tasks with variable steps; this task's steps are fixed | Suits large or paraphrase-heavy corpora; ours is ~100 authored facts | | Evaluability | Each stage has typed I/O and can be scored alone. Clean A–D ablation | Control flow varies per run, so component attribution and ablation get murky | Adds an embedding-model variable to every result | | Determinism and reproducibility | Only 3 LLM calls, all cached | Variable number of calls; loops; harder to cache | Index depends on the embedding model version | | Latency and cost | 3 calls, bounded | Unbounded calls; more tokens per step | +1 embedding call, or a local model | | Safety in a consequential domain | Rules can't be "skipped" by the model | Model may skip a rule check or retrieval | Same as RAG | | Dependencies | pydantic, pyyaml, BM25 lib | Agent framework (forbidden by REQ-ARC-002) | Vector store + embedding stack (torch ≈ 2 GB image, or an API) | | Assessment alignment | Matches the approved design; justifies complexity through ablation | Conflicts with REQ-ARC-002 / BD-09 | "Unnecessary vector databases" are excluded (REQ-ARC-002) | **Verdict:** the rules + BM25 pipeline. Neither alternative gives a testable benefit at this corpus size, and both are excluded by approved decisions. ### 4.2 Retrieval methods | Method | Strength | Weakness for this corpus | Cost | |---|---|---|---| | **BM25 (recommended)** | Exact matching on policy vocabulary (HFE, FT(PMC), "occupier", "core occupier", "nine months"); explainable scores; deterministic; zero model dependency; sub-millisecond on ~100 docs | Lexical mismatch: "fiancée" vs "fiance", "BTO" vs "new flat", colloquial questions | ~0 | | Semantic (dense embeddings) | Paraphrase matching | Weak on acronyms and numbers; needs torch (≈2 GB image, slow cold start) or an embedding API (another provider, data leaves); version drift | Medium | | Hybrid (BM25 + dense, RRF) | Best of both on large, varied corpora | Both dependencies; tuning a fusion weight on ~100 docs overfits the dev set | Medium–high | | Reranking (cross-encoder or LLM) | Precision at top ranks | Precision isn't the bottleneck: rule-linked facts are always included and k can be generous (~8 facts ≈ 600 tokens). An LLM reranker adds a call | Medium–high | **Recommendation: BM25 only**, with three cheap, deterministic mitigations for its known weakness: 1. **A curated `aliases` field on each fact**, indexed with the statement (e.g. "HDB Flat Eligibility", "HFE letter"; "fiance", "fiancée", "fiancé"). **[APPROVAL A2]**, a one-field schema addition to 03 §2.5. 2. **A topic filter:** search only facts whose topic passed the gate. 3. **Rule-linked facts always included** (stage ⑤). **Testable trigger for anything more:** - On the **dev** retrieval queries, if recall@5 falls below 0.90, *and* error analysis attributes the misses to paraphrase rather than coverage gaps, propose dense or hybrid retrieval as a decision, with before/after recall@k. - Otherwise, don't build it. **Alternative considered and not recommended: put the whole KB in the prompt.** At ~100 facts, it fits in context and removes retrieval failure. But it: - removes the explicit evidence set that the verifier and citations depend on; - scales badly; - inflates per-call cost; - turns config B into something other than RAG. **Implementation choice:** `rank-bm25` (small, pure Python, numpy only). The alternative is about 50 lines in-house; recommended only if you prefer zero dependencies. Tokeniser: lowercase, alphanumeric tokens, numbers kept, a small stop-word list, no stemming library. ## 5. Privacy and licensing in the design - **Fictional data only:** - the UI shows a banner: "Do not enter real personal information"; - user text is **not logged** by default; - the response cache is used only by eval runs on fictional cases. - **Provider data terms:** some free tiers allow providers to use inputs for training. That's acceptable for fictional benchmark data, **not** for real applicants. Record it as a deployment risk (REQ-PRIV-010) and as a model-selection criterion (Q-13: add privacy to the scorecard). - **Licensing:** - the runtime reads only authored facts; - the HDB pages are linked, not reproduced; - infographics and videos are links only (REQ-SRC-010/011); - `data/private_corpus/` is never imported. A unit test asserts that no runtime module references the path. - **Secrets:** API keys come from the environment only; there's a `.env.example` with placeholder names; the pre-push scan from CLAUDE.md applies. ## 9.
